Leve ao forno a gratinar cerca de 10 minutos na potencia máxima (forno já pré-aquecido).

name: Peru assado no forno: a nossa receita

ingredients.name: Sumo e raspa de laranja (ou limão)
Batata ou batata doce às rodelas

steps: Numa picadora ou com ajuda da varinha mágica coloquem azeite, o alho, a salsa, o colorau, o sumo (e raspa de laranja), o sal e a pimenta. Pique até obter uma “pasta”.
Num tabuleiro de ir ao forno coloque a perna de peru num tabuleiro e barre bem com “pasta”. Cubra com película e reserve no frio por algumas horas (preferencialmente no dia anterior.)
Pré aqueça o forno a 180ºC.
Junte as cebolas em meias luas e regue com vinho branco.
Leve ao forno por cerca de 1:30 (vá controlando) e vá cobrindo com molho.
Sirva com batata doce (ou normal) cozida ou assada. Pode se quiser juntar ao tabuleiro do peru 15 minutos antes de retirar do forno.

name: Nuggets de frango saudáveis
steps: Pré-aqueça o forno a 200ºC.
Coloque os cubinhos de frango numa taça e os restantes ingredientes para a marinada. Deixe marinar, pelo menos por 30 minutos.
Triture grosseiramente os flocos de milho.
Passe os cubos de frango um a um na mistura da crosta, pressionando bem para agarrar a crosta e coloque-os num tabuleiro forrado com papel vegetal
Leve-os ao forno, cerca de 10 a 15 minutos. No final sirva com umas gotas de limão.

name: A melhor quinoa que já fiz! (com bifes na frigideira com azeite e alho)
steps: Demolhe previamente a quinoa (pelo menos durante 12h) e deite fora a água.
Coloque a quinoa num tachinho, com o dobro da água, e coza por cerca de 10 a 15min (até fica translúcida e os “fios” ficarem brancos”).
Junte o açafrão, os legumes e envolva bem com um garfo. Deixe cozinhar por alguns minutos.
Rectifique temperos e está pronta a ser.
Numa frigideira coloque um fio de azeite. Descarregue a fúria do dia-a-dia e “esmurre” 2 dentes de alho e coloque os na frigideira. Junte a folha de louro.
Na hora, coloque sal nos bifes e coloque-os na frigideira.
Para mim, basta ficarem cerca de 30 segundos de cada lado (eram bem fininhos – Para o Lourenço deixei mais alguns segundos). Bom apetite!

name: Tortilha no forno de courgete e cogumelos
steps: Pré-aqueça o forno a 180 °C.
Coloque um fio de azeite numa frigideira com um dente de alho esmagado e salteie os cogumelos.
Adicione os pimentos e a curgete em cubos e deixe alourar.
Acrescente os orégãos e o tomilho.
Retire do lume e coloque num tabuleiro de levar ao forno.
Numa taça, bata os ovos com o iogurte, o polvilho e o fermento. Mexa bem e adicione ao tabuleiro.
Misture bem com a ajuda dum garfo.
Leve ao forno cerca de 20 a 25 minutos ou até dourar.

name: Croquetes de carne no forno!

ingredients.name: de chávena de flocos de trigo sarraceno (pode usar aveia)
farinha de amêndoa para moldar (ou farinha de linhaça, ou farelo de aveia ou pão ralado)

steps: Pré-aqueça o forno a 180ºC
Num robô de cozinha ou picadora coloque a vitela, a cebola, as sementes, os flocos de trigo sarraceno, o tomilho, os oregãos e um fio de azeite. Triture bem.
Se quiser congelar o preparado coloque numa caixa e leve ao congelador.
Numa taça bata os ovos e tempere com sal e pimenta a gosto.
Junte ao preparado de carne e mexa bem.
Junte farinha de amêndoa e vá moldando até ficar com formato de bolinhas. No final do “panar” com mais farinha de amêndoa.
Coloque num tabuleiro forrado com papel vegetal e leve ao forno até estarem tostadinhos.

name: Legumes na air fryer o nosso “medicamento” preferido

ingredients.name: Grão (previamente cozido e congelado por nós)

steps: Partimos tudo em cubos e temperamos com uma pitada de sal, orégãos e tomilho.
No grão adicionamos também uma pitada de cominhos e um fio generoso de azeite.

Distribui-se a mistura na Air Fryer, preferencialmente em duas fornadas para não sobrecarregar. Programa-se a 180ºC por cerca de 15 a 20 minutos, mexendo a meio do tempo para garantir uma cozedura uniforme.
Guardamos no frigorífico e vamos comendo.

name: Bolinhas de frango, queijo e azeitonas
steps: Pre-aqueça o forno a 200º C.
Numa taça, coloque todos os ingredientes e amasse bem até ligarem.
Faça pequenas bolas e coloque num tabuleiro de levar ao forno forrado com papel vegetal.
Leve ao forno cerca de 15-20 minutos.

name: “Frittata” de batata doce, mais uma pizza saudável
steps: No robô de cozinha, comece por ralar uma batata doce, adicione o queijo ralado, 1 ovo, o tomilho e os oregãos e mexa bem. Adicione um fio de azeite para ligar. (pode temperar com sal e pimenta, mas atenção que o queijo ralado já tem sal).
Numa frigideira que possa ir ao forno, coloque um fio de azeite e adicione o preparado. Coloque os tomate mini chucha partidos, e as mini mozzarella. Deixe cozinhar um pouco.
Polvilhe com mais um pouco de queijo ralado e leve ao forno por cerca de 5 minutos.
Coloque rúcula por cima e bom apetite!

name: Pizza saudável
steps: Pré-aqueça o forno a 180ºC.
Comece por triturar a couve flor cozida.
Adicione um ovo e o queijo ralado, e mexa até obter uma consistência homogénea.
Forre um tabuleiro com papel vegetal, e disponha/estique a massa. Leve ao forno por cerca de 10 minutos
Comece por colocar o molho de tomate, os óregãos e o queijo ralado.
Disponha os restantes ingredientes a gosto e leve ao forno por 10 a 15 minutos.
No final, coloque a rúcula por cima e bom apetite!

name: “Empadão” de vitela e couve flor
steps: Coloque num tacho o azeite e a cebola largamente picada, deixe alourar um pouco. Ao mesmo tempo, num tachinho coloque a couve flor a cozer.
Adicione o louro, a cenoura e o tomate partido aos pedaços. Vá mexendo. Adicione a carne e cubra com um pouco de água. Deixe cozer.
Pré-aqueça o forno a 180ºC.
Quando a carne estiver cozida, deixe o molho reduzir um pouco.
Coloque a carne num tabuleiro juntamente com a couve flor cozida, envolva bem e coloque queijo por cima. Leve ao forno até estar dourado.

name: Açorda de aveia e pescada
steps: Em primeiro lugar, coza a pescada e os ovos, em tachos separados.
De seguida, num tacho à parte, refogue os alhos e os talos dos coentros em azeite.
Depois, adicione a curgete cortada em cubos e deixe alourar durante alguns minutos.
Junte a aveia demolhada e a água da cozedura da pescada. Deixe cozinhar até atingir a consistência desejada.
Por fim, acrescente os ovos cozidos partidos, a pescada lascada e os coentros frescos. Tempere com flor de sal e, se gostar, um pouco de pimenta.

name: Arroz de couve flor com frango e pimentos
steps: Coloque na frigideira, o azeite e a cebola picada, deixe alourar.
Adicione os pimentos partidos em cubos e tempere com orégãos e tomilho. Deixe ganhar sabor e soltar um pouco da água dos pimentos.
Pique a couve flor e reserve.
Adicione as tiras de frango e deixe cozinhar. (Pode temperar as tiras de frango previamente com sal e pimenta).
Adicione a couve flor previamente picada e envolva bem. Prove, retifique os temperos e bom apetite 🙂

name: “Empadão” de carne e pimentos
steps: Numa frigideira, coloque o azeite e a cebola partida em rodelas. Deixe alourar um pouco.
Adicione os pimentos partidos em tiras e deixe alourar bem. Adicione o peito de peru e deixe cozinhar.
Pré-aqueça o forno a 180ºC.
Tempere com sal, pimenta e orégãos. E deixe cozinhar por cerca de 10 minutos.
Entretanto, comece a preparar a polenta, de acordo com as instruções na embalagem de sêmola de milho.
Num tabuleiro para o forno, disponha a carne e a polenta por camadas. Polvilhe com queijo ralado. Leve ao forno, 180º, por 10 a 15 minutos.

name: Jardineira de vitela

ingredients.name: vagens de feijão verde redondo (ou simplesmente feijão verde)

steps: Coloque a vitela a cozer num tachinho com água.
Num tacho ou robot de cozinha coloque os legumes (em cubos mais pequenos ou rodelas), a batata doce, as cenouras, a couve lombarda, o feijão frade e a cebola.
Leve a cozer por cerca de 15/20 minutos (até a couve estar bem cozida).
Quando a vitela estiver cozida, retire, triture e reserve.

Após os 15/20 min, adicione a vitela já triturada e consoante a consistência que pretender, triture mais, ou menos os legumes e a vitela. Não se esqueça de adicionar o azeite quando for servir a sopinha. Bom apetite!

name: Salmão no forno com massa folhada

ingredients.name: lombinhos de salmão (ou 3 postas de salmão se conseguir retirar as espinhas e a pele)

steps: Pré-aqueça o forno a 180ºC.
Parta os lombos de salmão em cubos e reserve.
Numa taça, coloque os espinafres e por cima esfarele o queijo feta e envolva bem.
Abra a massa folhada, coloque num tabuleiro e pique a base com um garfo.
Coloque o salmão sobre a massa folhada, e por cima do salmão coloque a mistura dos espinafres e do queijo feta. Coloque de forma a conseguir enrolar ou cobrir tudo com a massa folhada.
Leve ao forno por cerca de 20 minutos e bom apetite!

name: One-Tray Caramelized Onion & Garlic Pasta

ingredients.name: natas ou leite de coco (à temperatura ambiente)

steps: Pré-aqueça o forno a 200°C. Coloque as cebolas fatiadas num tabuleiro de forno. Tempere com colorau, alho em pó, sal, pimenta, tempero italiano e 4 colheres de sopa de azeite. Misture bem.
Corte o topo da cabeça de alho (cerca de 1 cm), regue com 1 colher de sopa de azeite, polvilhe com sal e coloque com o lado cortado para cima sobre as cebolas.

Cubra com papel de alumínio e leve ao forno durante 1 hora, mexendo as cebolas a cada 20 minutos. Em cada mexida, acrescente um pouco de água para evitar que queimem. Pretende-se cebolas douradas e caramelizadas.
Enquanto isso, coza a massa conforme as instruções da embalagem. Reserve até 1 chávena de água da cozedura antes de escorrer.
Retire o alho do tabuleiro e deixe arrefecer ligeiramente. Esprema os dentes de alho assado diretamente sobre as cebolas.

Adicione o chili crisp, as natas (ou leite de coco), o molho de soja (se usar), o sumo de limão, o parmesão e a massa cozida. Envolva tudo, adicionando água da cozedura conforme necessário até obter um molho brilhante e cremoso. Acerte o sal.
Finalize com mais parmesão, chili crisp e salsa fresca a gosto. Sirva com frango, camarão ou tofu.

name: Creamy Spinach Lentils with Burst Tomatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Add the cherry tomatoes to a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil and season well with salt and black pepper. Slide into the oven to roast for 15 mins, or until the tomatoes are soft, blistered and starting to burst.
Meanwhile, pour boiling water over the spinach in a sieve set in the sink. Once fully wilted, leave to cool slightly, then squeeze out as much liquid as you can and set aside.
Finely chop the shallots and garlic. Pick the thyme leaves from the stems. Drain and rinse the lentils.

Heat another drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Add the shallots and garlic with a pinch of salt and cook for 5 to 7 mins, until soft and translucent. Add the thyme leaves and cook for another couple of minutes until fragrant.

Tip the lentils into the pan and stir to warm through, then add the spinach. Pour in the double cream and let everything gently bubble into a loose, creamy sauce. Taste and adjust with salt and black pepper.
Spoon the creamy lentils onto plates and finish with the burst tomatoes on top. Get stuck in!

name: BLT Chicken Salad
steps: Butterfly the chicken breasts and season them generously with salt and pepper.
Add the bacon to a frying pan and place over a medium heat. Cook for 4–5 mins, until crispy and golden on both sides. Transfer to a plate, keeping the fat in the pan.
Add the chicken breasts to the same pan. Cook for 10–15 mins, flipping occasionally, until golden and cooked through.

Meanwhile, pick the parsley leaves and discard the stems. Chop the tomatoes (for the salad) into bite-sized chunks. Remove any tough kale stalks and add the leaves to a large bowl. Season with salt and massage for a couple of minutes until soft and wilted.

Make the dressing. Halve the tomato and coarsely grate the cut side into a bowl, discarding the skins. Crumble in half of the cooked bacon. Stir through the olive oil and season with salt, black pepper and a splash of sherry vinegar, to taste.
Add the parsley, chopped tomatoes, quinoa and tomato dressing to the bowl of kale. Toss everything together until well combined.

Slice the cooked chicken breasts. Share the salad between Tupperware containers and top with the chicken. Finish with the remaining crumbled bacon and a generous crack of black pepper. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Spicy Pork Rice Bowl with Sesame Broccoli
steps: Finely grate the garlic and mix it with the gochujang, oyster sauce, dark soy sauce and sugar in a small bowl. Set aside.
Place a large frying pan over a high heat with the vegetable oil. Once hot, add the pork mince and cook for 5–7 mins, breaking it up with a spoon as you go, until golden and caramelised.
Pour in the sauce and stir through. Cook for another 2–3 mins until thick, glossy and sticky.
Meanwhile, microwave the tenderstem broccoli for 2 mins until just tender. Toss with a pinch of salt, the sesame oil and the sesame seeds. Alternatively, steam or pan-fry if you prefer.
Trim and thinly slice the spring onions.
Spoon the rice into containers. Top with the pork, sesame broccoli and a scattering of spring onions and extra sesame seeds. Leave to cool and pop in the fridge until needed.

name: Gochujang Tofu "Mince" Rice Bowl
steps: Pat the tofu dry, then crumble it into small mince-sized pieces with your hands.
Heat the sesame oil in a large non-stick pan over a medium-high heat. Add the tofu and cook for 5–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned and crispy at the edges.
Grate the garlic and ginger — no need to peel. Peel and cut the carrot into matchsticks, and slice the cucumber into thin matchsticks too. Finely slice the spring onions, pick the mint leaves.

In a small bowl, mix together the gochujang, soy sauce, honey, garlic, gochujang, ginger and water. Pour the sauce into the pan with the crispy tofu. Stir-fry for a couple of minutes until glossy and well-coated.
Heat the rice according to the packet instructions, then spoon it into your Tupperware containers. Top with the gochujang tofu “mince,” edamame, carrot, and cucumber.
Finish with spring onion, lime wedges, mint and sesame seeds, if using. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Tofu Gyros Bowl
steps: Use a vegetable peeler to shave the tofu into ribbons. In a bowl, mix together the olive oil, smoked paprika, oregano, garlic powder, cumin, and a good pinch of salt and pepper. Add the tofu and toss to coat. Leave to marinate for at least 15 mins.
Air-fry the tofu at 190°C for 10 mins, or bake at 200°C for 10-15 mins, until golden and slightly crisp.

Meanwhile, dice the cucumber, halve the cherry tomatoes, and finely slice the red onion. Cut the lemon into wedges. Add the veg to a bowl and squeeze over ½ the lemon, saving the rest for serving. Cook the quinoa according to the packet instructions, then fluff it up with a fork and season lightly with salt and pepper.

Swoosh the Greek yoghurt into a Tupperware container. Pile on the quinoa, crispy tofu, cucumber, tomatoes, and red onion. Crumble over the feta and scatter with mint leaves. Serve with lemon wedges on the side for squeezing. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — it’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Miso Maple Chicken with Rice
steps: Butterfly the chicken breasts and season both sides with salt and pepper. Crush the garlic cloves, discarding the skins.
Stir the maple syrup, soy sauce, miso and water together in a small bowl. Set aside.

Thinly slice the cucumber. Defrost the edamame. Fill a kettle and bring to the boil. Add the spinach to a colander and pour over the boiling water until wilted. Let it cool slightly, then squeeze out any excess water.
Tip the sliced cucumber into a bowl, season with salt and set aside.
Place a frying pan over a medium heat and add the olive oil. Pat the chicken dry, then place into the pan. Cook for 8–10 mins, flipping halfway, until golden on both sides.
Add the garlic and pour in the miso-maple mixture. Let it bubble away, basting the chicken as it cooks, until the sauce thickens into a glossy glaze and the chicken is cooked through.
Reheat the rice. Stir the edamame, spinach, rice vinegar and sesame seeds through the cucumber to make the salad.

Share the rice between Tupperware containers and top with the glazed chicken and crunchy salad. Spoon over any leftover glaze from the pan. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch - they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Honey Mustard Pork Chop & Garlicky Beans
steps: Season the pork chops generously with salt and pepper on both sides, then set aside. Pick the parsley leaves and finely slice the soft stems. Gently crush the garlic for the pork and set aside.
Finely grate the garlic for the beans into a saucepan. Add the parsley stems and chickpeas (with their liquid), then set over a medium heat and let it gently simmer until ready to serve.

Crush the garlic for the pork, discarding the skins. Pat the chops dry. Add the olive oil to a frying pan and place the pork chops fat-side down. Set over a medium-high heat and let the fat render for 3–4 mins. Once browned, sear both sides of the chops for 5–6 mins until golden and cooked through. Transfer to a plate to rest.

Pour the chicken stock into the empty pan and add the crushed garlic. Let it bubble and reduce by half, then take it off the heat and stir through the honey and wholegrain mustard. Taste and season with salt, pepper and a splash of sherry vinegar.

Slice the pork chops and stir any resting juices into the sauce. Spoon the garlicky beans into Tupperware containers, top with the pork, then drizzle over the sauce. Finish with a scattering of parsley leaves. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Seared Tuna & Olive Grains
steps: Season the tuna steaks with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Finely dice the shallot and add to a bowl with the juice of the lemon. Stir in the honey, oregano and a pinch of salt. Whisk in the olive oil to make your dressing.
Finely mince the olives, sundried tomatoes and roasted peppers. Stir into the dressing, then add the hot grains and toss well to coat.
Bring a saucepan of water to the boil. Once boiling, reduce to a medium heat, gently lower in the eggs and cook for 7 mins until jammy. Transfer to an ice bath, leave to cool, then peel.

Place a frying pan over a high heat with the remaining olive oil. Once hot, add the tuna steaks and sear on both sides until golden and just cooked through. Transfer to a board to rest for a couple of minutes.

Toss the grains and parsley leaves together, then divide between Tupperware containers. Slice the tuna and halve the eggs, then top both onto the grain mix. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Sticky Pomegranate Glazed Chicken & Herby Quinoa
steps: Stir the Lebanese 7-spice and 1 tablespoon of olive oil together in a large bowl. Season with salt and pepper, then toss the chicken thighs through the marinade. Set aside to marinate.
Cook the quinoa following pack instructions. Once done, set aside to cool slightly.

Finely mince the parsley and coriander (stalks and all). Tip into a bowl with the quinoa and pomegranate seeds. Roughly crush the walnuts and add those in too. Stir through the olive oil, season with salt, and squeeze over the juice of the lemon. Give everything a good mix and adjust the seasoning to taste.
Set a frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the chicken thighs and cook for 10–15 mins, turning halfway, until golden and cooked through.
Pour in the pomegranate molasses and honey. Take the pan off the heat and baste the chicken in the sticky glaze for a minute or two until coated and glossy.

Spoon the quinoa salad into Tupperware containers. Top with the glazed chicken and any juices from the pan. Serve with any leftover lemon wedges on the side. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Herby Grilled Salmon Quinoa Bowl
steps: Finely slice the dill and chives, keeping them separate. Thinly slice the cucumber and red onion. Tip the cucumber into a bowl, season with salt and stir through the vinegar.
Wash the red onion under cold water until crisp. Stir the chives through the cottage cheese and season with salt and black pepper.

Bring a saucepan of water to the boil. Once boiling, gently drop in the eggs and cook for 7 mins until jammy — or a little longer if you prefer them firmer. Transfer to a bowl of ice water to cool, then peel.

Place a frying pan over a medium heat with the olive oil. Once hot, add the salmon skin-side down and cook undisturbed until it’s about three-quarters of the way done. Remove from the heat and flip to finish cooking through.
Reheat the quinoa and stir through the dill. Season with salt and grate in the zest of the lemon. Toss the red onion through the cucumber just before serving.

Divide the quinoa between Tupperware containers. Top with the crispy salmon, a jammy egg, a dollop of herby cottage cheese and a pile of cucumber salad. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Edamame Hummus & Quinoa Bowl
steps: Cook the eggs in a small saucepan of boiling water for 7 mins, until jammy in the centre. Drain and cool under cold running water until easy to peel.
Boil the peas and edamame in salted water according to pack instructions. Drain and run under cold water to stop the cooking.
Zest and juice the lemons. Peel the garlic.
Add half of the edamame and peas to a food processor along with the cottage cheese, tahini, lemon zest and juice, garlic and water. Season with salt and black pepper, then blitz until super smooth.

Warm the quinoa following pack instructions, or use cold if you prefer. Tip it into a bowl with the remaining edamame and peas. Finely chop most of the mint and stir it through the quinoa. Season well with salt and pepper.

To serve, spread the hummus into Tupperware containers. Spoon the quinoa salad on top, then halve the eggs and place them on top too. Crumble over the feta and finish with the reserved mint leaves. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Beef & Udon Noodle Stir-Fry
steps: Thinly slice the steak and season with a little salt and plenty of black pepper. Thinly slice the chilli and cut the spring onions into four pieces each. Peel and thinly slice the garlic. Peel the ginger and cut into matchsticks.
Place a wok or large deep frying pan over a medium-high heat with the sunflower oil. Once hot, add the steak and cook for 1-2 mins per side until just browned, then move it to one side of the pan.
Add the spring onions to the empty side of the pan and stir-fry for 1 min until fragrant. Add the chilli, garlic and ginger and toss for 1 min.
Chuck in the stir-fry veg and toss everything together. Cook for 2 mins until the veg starts to soften.
Add the udon noodles and toss again. Pour in the soy sauce, honey and the juice of half the lime. Stir-fry for another 1-2 mins until everything is piping hot.
Divide between Tupperware containers and top with the coriander, if using. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch – they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Greek Halloumi & Lentil Bowl
steps: Cut the courgette into chunks. Chop the mint, setting aside a few leaves to garnish later. Cut the halloumi into 2cm chunks.

Chuck the courgette into the drawer of an air fryer. Spritz with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, then cook at 200°C for 15 mins. Toss in the cherry tomatoes, dried oregano and halloumi for the final 6 mins.
Peel the garlic. Zest the lemon, then juice it.
Blitz the garlic, cottage cheese, Dijon mustard, lemon zest and juice in a blender with enough water to make a drizzling consistency (start with a tablespoon). Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Drain the lentils and chickpeas and tip them into a large bowl. Toss with the chopped mint and half the dressing.

Spoon the salad into Tupperware containers, top with the roasted halloumi and tomatoes, drizzle with the remaining dressing and garnish with the reserved mint leaves. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Tempeh Burrito Bowl with Black Beans & Salsa
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C.
If making a tortilla bowl, press the wrap into an ovenproof bowl to form a bowl shape. Bake for 10 mins until golden and crisp, then remove and cool. Or, simply serve with tortilla for scooping.
Heat the rice according to pack instructions. Drain and rinse the black beans, then stir them through the rice with a pinch of salt and black pepper. Set aside.

Peel and finely dice the onion. Halve the tomato, scoop out the seeds, then finely dice the flesh. Chop the coriander and combine it all in a bowl with the juice of half the lime and a pinch of salt and pepper. Slice the roasted peppers.

Crumble the tempeh into mince-sized pieces. Heat a drizzle of oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the tempeh and fry for 5–6 mins until golden and crisp. Add the paprika, cumin and chilli powder, then stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.

To build your bowl, spoon in the rice and beans, top with the spiced tempeh, fresh salsa and sliced roasted peppers. Finish with a dollop of yoghurt, a scattering of coriander and a lime wedge on the side. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Lentil Tofu Ragù & Chickpeas
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C
Crumble the tofu with your hands into mince-sized chunks. Tip onto a lined baking tray, season with salt and pepper. Roast for 15 mins until starting to char, then set aside.
Finely chop the carrot, celery, onion and garlic. Heat oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the chopped veg and a pinch of salt. Cook for 10–15 mins until soft and starting to caramelise.
Stir in the tomato purée and cook for 2 mins to darken and intensify.
Drain the chickpeas and lentils. Add both to the pan along with the chopped tomatoes, miso, tofu and stock. Season again, then simmer for 15–20 mins until thickened.
Roughly chop the parsley. Serve topped with parsley. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Beef Kofte with Tahini-Rippled Greek Yoghurt
steps: Heat the grill to high. Add the dried fruit and nut mix to a food processor and pulse until finely chopped. Tip out a small spoonful to use as a garnish later.
Pick the parsley leaves and add all but a few leaves to the food processor. Pulse to finely chop. Add the beef mince, za'atar, a good pinch of salt and black pepper, then pulse to just combine.
Use your hands to mix everything together, then shape into logs about 11cm long. Transfer to a foil-lined baking tray and grill for 6-8 mins, turning halfway, until golden and cooked through.

Meanwhile, finely slice the red onion and add to a bowl with the red wine vinegar or lemon juice and a good pinch of salt. Scrunch together with your hands and leave for 5 mins to pickle. Dice the cucumber and radishes. Then toss through the cucumber, radishes. Season to taste.

Warm the flatbreads in a dry pan. Spread the Greek yoghurt over the warm flatbreads, then drizzle with tahini. Top with the salad and kofte. Scatter over the reserved parsley and dried fruit mix to finish.

name: Creamy Sun-Dried Tomato Pasta Salad
steps: Bring a pot of salted water to the boil and cook the pasta according to the packet instructions until al dente. Drain, reserving a splash of the pasta water, and leave to cool slightly. Finely chop the sun-dried tomatoes and garlic.
While the pasta cooks, heat the sun-dried tomato oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and chopped sun-dried tomatoes, cooking gently for 1–2 mins until fragrant.
Pop the spinach into a colander or sieve and pour over two kettles of boiling water to wilt it. Squeeze out any excess moisture.

Stir the cottage cheese, pasta, wilted spinach, and most of the basil through the sun-dried tomato mix. Add a splash of the reserved pasta water if needed to loosen, and season well with salt and pepper.
Serve topped with Parmesan shavings and the remaining basil. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Cajun-Spiced Chicken Meatball & Butternut Chilli
steps: Mix the chicken mince with half of the Cajun seasoning, then shape into small balls.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over a medium-high heat. Add the chicken meatballs and fry for about 5 mins until browned on all sides.

Add the sofrito mix and cook, stirring, for 2 mins. Finely slice the garlic and chuck it in with the chopped butternut squash. Cook for 1 min, then stir through the Cajun seasoning and cook for another minute until fragrant.

Pour in the plum tomatoes, squashing them with the back of a spoon. Fill one of the empty cans with water, swirl and tip into the pan. Add the beans — liquid and all — then bring everything to a simmer.
Turn the heat down and cook for 30 mins until thickened and the squash is soft. Stir through the balsamic and season to taste with salt and black pepper. Grate the cheddar and pick the coriander.

Ladle the chilli into Tupperware containers and top with a dollop of Greek yoghurt, fresh coriander leaves and a little extra Cajun seasoning. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Creamy Tomato Gnocchi Bake
steps: Heat your grill to high. Bring a small pan of salted water to the boil and cook the gnocchi for about 2 mins, until they float. Drain and set aside. Halve the cherry tomatoes.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and fry for 2 mins until fragrant. Add the tomato purée and cook for another minute before adding the cherry tomatoes.
Mix well, then take the pan off the heat and stir in the chickpeas and cottage cheese until everything is combined. Season with salt and pepper.
If you’re not using an ovenproof frying pan, transfer the mix to a baking dish. Top with the parmesan and slide under the grill for 3–5 mins until golden and bubbling.
Scatter over the torn basil and serve straight away.

name: Smoky Tempeh Breakfast Bowl
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Rinse the quinoa under cold water, then cook in a pan of salted boiling water for 12–15 mins until fluffy. Drain and set aside.
Slice the tempeh and chuck it into a bowl with the smoked paprika, soy sauce, maple syrup, half the olive oil and a pinch of black pepper. Toss to coat, then spread out on one side of a baking tray.

Toss the cherry tomatoes with the rest of the olive oil and some salt and pepper. Add to the other side of the tray, then slide it into the oven for 15 mins until the tomatoes are soft and blistered and the tempeh is golden.
Finely chop most of the parsley, saving a few leaves for garnish. Stir the chopped parsley through the cooked quinoa.

Grate the garlic and squeeze the lime. Add both to a blender with the edamame and a pinch of salt and pepper. Blitz until smooth, adding a splash of water if needed to loosen it to a hummus-like consistency.

Spoon the quinoa into a Tupperware container and top with the roasted tomatoes and crispy tempeh. Add a big dollop of the edamame guac and finish with the rest of the parsley. Serve with a wedge of lime on the side, if you like. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Chargrilled Chicken & Garlicky Broccoli Rice
steps: Finely chop the garlic. Chop the broccoli into small florets, smaller than you would usually.
Add half the olive oil to a large saucepan with a lid and set over a medium heat. Chuck in the garlic and cook for a couple of minutes until fragrant.
Tip in the rice and pour in the chicken stock. Bring to the boil, then cover with the lid, reduce the heat to low and cook for 4 mins.

After 4 mins, scatter the broccoli over the top. Give everything a quick stir, replace the lid and cook for another 8 mins. Turn off the heat and leave the rice to steam for 10 mins while you crack on with the chicken.

Place one of the chicken breasts between two sheets of baking paper and bash it with a rolling pin until about 1cm thick. Repeat with the rest of the chicken. Add the flattened chicken to a bowl with the remaining olive oil, ground cumin, a generous pinch of salt and pepper. Toss to coat.

Heat a large frying pan over a high heat. Once hot, add the chicken and cook for 3-4 mins on each side until well charred and cooked through. Transfer to a piece of foil, squeeze over the juice of the lemon and loosely seal to keep warm.
Finely chop the dill and stir it through the rice. Taste and season with more salt and pepper if needed.

Slice the chicken and serve it over the rice in Tupperware containers with a generous dollop of cottage cheese. Grate over a little lemon zest if you fancy. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Piri Piri Chicken & Herby Lemon Chickpeas
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Bash the chicken breasts between two sheets of baking paper until about 1cm thick. Drizzle with half the olive oil, sprinkle over the piri piri seasoning and season well with salt and pepper.
Transfer to a baking tray lined with foil and bake for about 12 mins, or until fully cooked. Set aside then slice before serving.
Meanwhile, finely slice the garlic. Using a vegetable peeler, peel off a few strips of lemon zest. Finely slice the red chilli, if using.

Heat the rest of the olive oil in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for a couple of minutes until just golden. Stir through the fennel seeds and chilli and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Pour in the chickpeas along with around half of their liquid, add the lemon zest strips and season well with salt and pepper. Mix, then cover with a lid and simmer gently for 10 mins.
Finely chop the parsley. Take the pan off the heat and stir through the Greek yoghurt and most of the chopped parsley.

Slice the cooked chicken and serve it in a Tupperware container on top of the creamy chickpeas. Finish with a bit more parsley if you fancy. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Creamy Green Pasta & Beans
steps: Drain and rinse the butter beans. Remove the cavolo nero leaves from their stems and roughly chop. Finely chop the garlic.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and cook the pasta following pack instructions. Once cooked, drain and reserve the cooking water.
While the pasta is cooking, heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 1-2 mins until fragrant.
Add the cavolo nero and edamame to the pan with a good pinch of salt. Pop a lid on and cook for 3-5 mins, until the leaves have wilted and the edamame is bright green.

Transfer the cooked greens to a blender with a couple of tablespoons of the butter beans and a splash of the pasta water. Blend until smooth, adding more water as needed to loosen. Season to taste with salt and black pepper.

Stir the green sauce through the pasta along with the remaining butter beans. Spoon into Tupperware containers and top with the basil and a crack of black pepper. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Tuna, Lentil & Feta Salad
steps: Peel and slice the red onion and add it to a large mixing bowl. Pour in the red wine vinegar, add the dried oregano, capers and olive oil, then season with salt and pepper. Whisk everything together to make a punchy dressing.
Finely chop the mint and stir it through the dressing.
Drain and rinse the lentils and butter beans, then chuck them into the bowl and toss well to coat.
Drain the tuna and crumble the feta.

Serve up the salad into Tupperware containers and top with the tuna and feta. Finish with a crack of black pepper. Box up and pop in the fridge, ready for when you need it. These keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Paprika Prawns & Garlicky Mashed Beans
steps: Zest the lemon and set aside. Thinly slice the chilli and half the garlic. Finely grate the remaining garlic. Pick the parsley leaves and finely slice the soft stalks.
Devein the prawns if you like, then set aside.
Place a saucepan over a medium heat. Pour in the beans with their liquid and add the grated garlic. Bring to the boil for 2-3 mins, then reduce to a low simmer while you cook the prawns.

Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the parsley stalks, sliced garlic and three-quarters of the chilli. Cook for 1-2 mins until softened, then chuck in the cherry tomatoes. Cook for 5-7 mins, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes burst.
Add the prawns and smoked paprika to the pan. Stir through and cook for 2-3 mins, until the prawns are cooked through. Season with salt, pepper, lemon zest and lemon juice.

Meanwhile, lightly mash the beans in the saucepan. Stir through the cottage cheese and season to taste with salt, pepper, lemon zest and more juice, if you like. Add a splash of water for a looser consistency.
Spoon the garlicky mashed beans into bowls. Top with the paprika prawns and pan juices. Finish with parsley leaves, the remaining chilli and a wedge of lemon on the side.

name: Curried Mango Chicken & Garlicky Rice with Greens
steps: Rinse the jasmine rice in a saucepan under cold water until it runs clear. Add the measured water and a big pinch of salt.

Bash the garlic cloves for the rice and remove their skins. Add them to the rice and place over a high heat. Bring to the boil, cover with a lid, then turn the heat down to low. Cook for 12 mins, then remove from the heat and leave to steam, lid on, for 10 mins.

Butterfly the chicken breasts. In a bowl, mix together the curry powder and half the olive oil. Season generously with salt and pepper, then toss the chicken through the marinade until well coated. Set aside.
Set a large frying pan over a medium heat with the remaining olive oil. Once hot, add the kale and cook for 2-3 mins until just wilted. Transfer to a plate.
Add the chicken to the empty pan and cook for 10-15 mins, turning halfway, until golden on both sides.
Finely grate the garlic and ginger into a small bowl. Stir through the mango chutney and water to make a loose sauce.
Once the chicken is golden, pour in the mango sauce and cook, basting, until it glazes the chicken and the meat is cooked through, 5-6 mins.
Use scissors to snip any large watercress into smaller pieces. Add it to the chicken with the kale, cover with a lid and leave to steam over low heat for 2-4 mins until the greens have wilted.

Fluff the rice with a fork and divide between Tupperware containers. Top with the glazed chicken, greens and any extra sauce from the pan. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Prawn & Mango Coconut Bowl
steps: Peel and dice the mango. Thinly dice the red onion. Add both to a bowl with the juice of half the limes and a pinch of salt. Stir and set aside to pickle.
Thinly slice the garlic. Devein the prawns, if needed. Pick half of the coriander leaves and finely chop the rest, including the stalks.

Set a frying pan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the desiccated coconut and toast it dry for 2–4 mins until golden. Tip into a small bowl and stir through the chilli flakes and crispy onions. Set aside.

Return the empty pan to a medium-high heat with the olive oil. Once hot, add the garlic and cook for 2–3 mins until fragrant and just golden. Tip in the prawns and cook for 2–4 mins, stirring occasionally, until pink and cooked through. Remove from the heat.
Meanwhile, reheat the rice. Stir through the finely chopped coriander and divide between bowls.

Spoon the garlicky prawns and mango salsa over the rice. Finish with a generous sprinkle of the coconut mixture and a scattering of the remaining coriander leaves. Serve with any leftover lime wedges.

name: Spicy, Herby Fish with Curried Orzo
steps: Add the garam masala to a bowl with half the olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Drop in the cod fillets and stir to coat evenly. Set aside.
Thinly slice the garlic, chilli and onion. Pick the basil leaves. Heat the grill to medium.
Heat the remaining oil in a large frying pan with high sides over a medium heat. Once hot, add the garlic, chilli and half the onion. Cook for 4–5 mins until softened.

Tip in the orzo and curry powder. Stir for a minute until fragrant, then pour in the stock and water. Bring to the boil, then lower the heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the orzo is al dente (check your pack for timings).

Place the cod onto a foil-lined tray and slide under the grill for 5–10 mins, until cooked through and lightly charred. If it’s colouring too quickly, move it down a shelf or turn the grill down slightly.
Stir the coconut milk through, until creamy. Season to taste with salt, pepper and a squeeze of lime juice. Add a splash of water into the orzo to loosen it, if needed.

Spoon the curried orzo into Tupperware containers and top with the grilled cod. Finish with a scattering of basil leaves, the remaining onion and chilli. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Chicken & Cauliflower Fried Rice Bowl
steps: Peel and finely slice the ginger into matchsticks. Peel and finely chop the garlic.

Heat half of the sesame oil in a large nonstick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the chicken mince and cook for about 4 mins, breaking it up with a wooden spoon until no longer pink. Add half the soy sauce and half the gochujang, stir to coat, then transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining sesame oil to the pan. Add the ginger and garlic and cook for 1 min until fragrant.

Tip in the frozen red peppers and edamame and stir-fry for 2–3 mins until heated through. Push everything to one side of the pan and spritz a little olive oil spray onto the empty space. Crack in the eggs and scramble them with a spoon, then fold through the veg.

Add the cooked chicken back to the pan along with the frozen cauliflower rice, remaining gochujang and soy sauce. Stir everything together and cook for 2–3 mins until piping hot. Season to taste. Pick the coriander leaves.

Spoon the rice into Tupperware containers, scatter over the coriander and serve with lime wedges. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Fragrant & Spicy Pork Bowl
steps: Thinly slice the bird’s-eye chillies and the shallot. Add both to a bowl with the juice of the limes, fish sauce and sugar. Mix it all together. It should be tangy, slightly sweet and savoury. Set aside.
Pick the mint leaves and discard the stems. Pick the coriander leaves and thinly slice the stems. Defrost the edamame and chop the cabbage into bite-sized chunks (2–3cm).

Heat a large frying pan or wok over a high heat with no oil. Once hot, chuck in the cabbage, season with salt and cook for 4–6 mins, stirring occasionally, until it’s wilted and starting to char. Tip it onto a plate and set aside.

Lower the heat to medium. Add the water, fish sauce, coriander stems and pork mince to the pan. Season with salt and black pepper, then cook, breaking up the mince as you go, until it’s just cooked through. It should be grey, not browned — that’s how you keep it juicy.
Reheat the rice following pack instructions and divide between bowls.

Stir the cabbage, edamame, dressing and most of the herbs through the pork. Spoon the mixture over the rice, then finish with a scattering of the remaining herbs and any leftover lime wedges. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Honey Sriracha Tofu Bowl
steps: Pat the tofu dry, then cut it into small cubes. Heat the sesame oil in a large non-stick pan over a medium-high heat. Add the tofu and cook for 8–10 mins until golden and crisp on all sides.
Grate the garlic and ginger – no need to peel. Slice the roasted red pepper into strips. Finely slice the spring onion and cut the lime into wedges for serving.
In a small bowl, whisk together the sriracha, honey, soy sauce, garlic, and ginger with 1-2 tablespoons of water to loosen. Add the yoghurt to a bowl with the kimchi and mix.
Pour the sauce into the pan with the crispy tofu and toss to coat. Let it bubble for 1–2 minutes until sticky and glossy.
Heat the rice according to the package instructions and add it to a Tupperware container. Top with the honey sriracha tofu, roasted red pepper and kimchi yoghurt.
Sprinkle over the peanuts and spring onion. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch – they’ll keep for up to 3 days. Serve with a lime wedge for squeezing

name: Spice-Crusted Tuna & Red Pepper Beans
steps: Finely dice the onion and thinly slice the garlic, zest the lemon. Drain the red peppers and finely chop them. Pick the parsley leaves and thinly slice the stems.
Cover the tuna steaks in the Cajun seasoning, pressing to coat all over. Season with salt and set aside.

Heat a saucepan over a medium heat with half the olive oil. Once hot, add the onion and cook, stirring, for 4–5 mins until soft and translucent. Add the garlic, parsley stems and tomato purée, then cook for 2–4 mins, stirring, until the purée darkens.

Tip in the white beans and their liquid, followed by the chopped red peppers. Season with salt and black pepper, then bring to the boil. Turn the heat down to low and let it simmer gently while you cook the tuna. Add a splash of water to loosen if needed.

Heat a frying pan over a medium-high heat with the remaining olive oil. Once hot, add the tuna steaks and sear for 3–5 mins on each side, or until nicely coloured and beginning to char. Remove from the heat and let them rest for a couple of minutes.

Taste the beans and adjust with more salt, pepper and lemon juice, if needed. Spoon the beans into your Tupperware containers. Slice the tuna and lay it over the top. Finish with a sprinkle of lemon zest, parsley leaves and any remaining lemon wedges on the side. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Tandoori Chicken with Tamarind Chickpea Salad
steps: Heat the grill to medium-high.
Finely grate the garlic into a bowl. Add the tandoori spice mix, Greek yoghurt, a pinch of salt and a few cracks of black pepper. Stir to combine into a marinade.
Butterfly the chicken breasts, then pop them between two sheets of baking parchment. Bash with a rolling pin until they’re about 1cm thick. Add the chicken to the marinade and toss to coat well.

Line a baking tray with foil and lay the chicken breasts flat on top, making sure all the marinade is spread over them. Slide under the grill for 10–15 mins until cooked through and starting to char. If they’re catching too fast, lower the tray or turn the grill down.
Meanwhile, dice the cucumber into 2cm chunks and chop the tomatoes into bite-sized pieces. Pick the mint leaves and discard the stems.
Whisk together the tamarind purée, honey and the juice of the lime in a small bowl. Season with salt to taste and tweak with more lime or honey, if needed.
Toss the chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes and mint with the tamarind dressing until well coated.

Spoon your salad into your Tupperware containers and top with the chicken. Finish with some freshly cracked black pepper and any remaining lime wedges. Box up and pop in the fridge, ready for when you need it. These keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Herby, Creamy Chicken Salad & Roast Potatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Wash and dry the potatoes, then chuck them onto a baking tray. Drizzle over one-third of the olive oil, rub it into the potatoes, season with salt and pepper, then roast for 20–25 mins until golden and cooked through.

Add the chicken breasts to a bowl with the garlic powder, onion powder and the remaining olive oil. Toss everything together, then lay the chicken on a lined baking tray and roast for 15–20 mins, until cooked through. Let it rest for a couple of minutes once done.
Meanwhile, zest the lemon. Thinly slice all of the chives. Thinly slice the celery and cucumber. Pick the parsley leaves and thinly slice the soft stems.

Chuck the cottage cheese into a blender with the chives, the parsley stems, garlic powder and onion powder. Blitz until smooth, then season with salt, pepper and a good squeeze of lemon juice. Stir through as much of the lemon zest as you like.

Finely dice the cooked chicken. Add it to a large bowl with the cottage cheese dressing, chopped celery, cucumber and half of the parsley leaves and remaining chives. Taste and adjust the seasoning with more salt, pepper, lemon juice or zest if needed.

Spoon the chicken salad into your Tupperware containers with the roast potatoes on the side. Finish with a drizzle of any remaining olive oil and a scattering of the rest of the chives and parsley. Box up and pop in the fridge, ready for when you need it. These keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Traybake Orange Chicken Noodles
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C.

Chop the cabbage into 2–3cm chunks. Chop the spring onion whites into 2cm pieces and thinly slice the greens. Thinly slice the chicken breasts, then toss in a bowl with the cornflour. Season well with salt and pepper.

Pour half the olive oil into a large baking tray and tilt to coat the base and sides. Tip in the chicken, cabbage and spring onion whites, drizzle over the remaining oil and season with salt and pepper, toss together. Slide into the oven for 10–15 mins, until the veggies have softened and the chicken is cooked.
Meanwhile, finely grate the garlic and ginger into a small bowl. Add the orange juice, soy sauce, vinegar, honey and cornflour. Stir to combine, then taste and season if needed.
Once the traybake is cooked, toss through the noodles and sauce. Return to the oven for another 5–10 mins until everything is hot and coated in the thickened sauce.

Toss once more before serving the noodles between plates. Finish with a scattering of spring onion greens. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Roasted Winter Veg & Chicken Salad
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C.

Slice the sweet potato into 1cm-thick rounds. Trim and halve the Brussels sprouts. Toss both with half the olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and roast for 20 mins until golden and tender. Drizzle with the maple syrup.
Meanwhile, add the apple cider vinegar to a bowl with the powdered peanut butter and 1 Tbsp water and whisk until you’ve got a drizzly dressing. Season to taste.

Season the chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Heat the remaining oil in a nonstick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 7–8 mins, turning halfway, until golden and cooked through. Set aside to rest for 1 min, then slice.
Tear the radicchio into bite-sized pieces and chuck it into a large bowl with the rocket. Add the roasted veg and toss with the dressing.

Spoon the salad into Tupperware containers, top with the sliced chicken, scatter with pomegranate seeds and crumble over the goats’ cheese. Box up and pop in the fridge, ready for when you need it. These keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Chicken & Cottage Cheese Meatballs with Butter Beans
steps: Heat the grill to high. Peel and finely grate the garlic. Pick the parsley leaves and finely chop them.

Chuck half the garlic and one-third of the chopped parsley into a mixing bowl with the chicken mince and cottage cheese. Grate over the zest of half the lemon and finely grate in half the Parmesan. Season well with salt and black pepper.
Shape into golfball-sized meatballs with wet hands and place them onto a foil-lined baking tray.
Grill the meatballs for about 15 mins, until golden and cooked through.

Meanwhile, dump the butter beans (liquid and all) into a small frying pan and bring to a simmer. Fold through the spinach to wilt. Tip any juices from the chicken into the beans and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Grate over the remaining lemon zest and squeeze in the juice from a quarter of the lemon. Cut the rest into wedges for serving.

Spoon the beans into Tupperware containers and top with the meatballs. Sprinkle over the remaining chopped parsley, garlic, and chilli flakes then grate over the remaining Parmesan. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch - they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Spicy Prawn Cocktail Salad
steps: Zest half the lemon and squeeze in ½ the juice (cut the remaining into wedges for serving). Blitz the cottage cheese, sriracha, lemon zest and juice in a blender until smooth and creamy. Transfer to a bowl, season with salt and pepper, and fold through the prawns.
Finely slice the cornichons and finely chop the spring onions. Stir most of them through the prawn mix, saving a few for garnish.
Wash and separate the baby gem leaves. Slice the avocado and quarter the cherry tomatoes.

Mound the lettuce into Tupperware containers and top with the prawns, avocado and cherry tomatoes. Top with the remaining cornichons and spring onions, then dust with paprika. Nestle in a little wedge of lemon. Box up and pop in the fridge, ready for when you need it. These keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Lemon Chicken & Orzo Soup
steps: Dice the carrot, onion, and carrot to create a veg base mix. Heat the olive oil in a medium saucepan over a medium heat. Add the veg base mix and cook until softened but not coloured, about 5 mins.
Peel and crush the garlic, then stir it through the veg for 1 min until fragrant. Pour in the chicken bone broth and bring everything to the boil.
Tip in the orzo, shred over the leftover chicken and add the chickpeas (including their liquid). And simmer for 7- 8  mins, stirring occasionally, until the orzo is tender.
Pick and roughly chop the dill, then stir it through the soup with plenty of black pepper.
Ladle into Tupperware containers. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days. Serve with lemon wedges for squeezing over the top.

name: Miso-Glazed Chicken with Sweet Potato & Edamame
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Peel and finely chop the garlic. Add it to a shallow bowl with the miso paste, soy sauce, honey and crunchy chilli oil. Whisk until smooth.
Score the chicken breasts in a criss-cross pattern to help the marinade sink in and speed up cooking. Add to the bowl and coat well. Transfer to a roasting tray.
Peel and cut the sweet potatoes into 3cm chunks, then toss them through the marinade.
Tip the potatoes into the roasting tray and slide into the oven. Roast for 18–20 mins, giving the sweet potato a toss halfway through.
With 5 mins to go, drizzle the broccoli with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Add the broccoli and edamame to the tray with the chicken and sweet potato.

Divide the sweet potato, edamame, broccoli and chicken between Tupperware containers. Scatter over the mint leaves and sesame seeds. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Tuna Caesar with Butternut Squash & Parmesan Crisps
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Chop the butternut squash into 5cm pieces, chuck onto a baking tray with half the olive oil, season with salt and black pepper, then roast for 20 mins or until tender and starting to colour.

Peel and finely grate the garlic into a mixing bowl. Mash the anchovies and garlic together using a fork to form a paste. Zest over half the lemon (save the rest for later), then squeeze in the juice. Add the yoghurt, Worcestershire sauce, Dijon mustard and plenty of black pepper. Whisk together, loosening with splashes of cold water until it’s as runny as you like.

Heat a nonstick frying pan over a medium heat. Finely grate the Parmesan directly into the pan in an even layer and cook until bubbling. Remove from the heat, let it cool for a couple of minutes, then gently lift the Parmesan crisp out. Once cool, snap into shards.
Strip the cavolo nero leaves from their stems and finely shred the leaves. Toss into a bowl with a pinch of salt and the remaining lemon juice. Scrunch it all together with your hands to soften.

Brush the tuna steaks with the remaining oil and season with salt and black pepper. Heat a large nonstick frying pan over a medium-high heat, then cook the tuna for 2 mins per side for a pink centre. Transfer to a plate to rest, then sprinkle over the reserved lemon zest.

Toss the roasted squash and lemony dressing through the cavolo nero, then divide between Tupperware containers. Slice the tuna and lay it on top, finishing with the Parmesan crisps. Box up and pop in the fridge, ready for when you need it. These keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Firecracker Beef Rice Bowl
steps: Rinse the rice under cold water 2–3 times until the water runs clear. Add it to a lidded saucepan with the water and a pinch of salt. Set over a medium heat. Once it starts to simmer, cover with the lid, reduce the heat to low and cook for 10 mins. Remove from the heat and leave to steam for 10 mins. Fluff with a fork.
Meanwhile, peel and finely slice the onion. Peel the garlic and ginger and grate both into a bowl. Add the sriracha, honey, soy sauce and rice vinegar, and stir to make your sauce.
Thinly slice the red chillies. Trim and finely slice the spring onions.
Set a large frying pan over a medium heat with the oil. Once hot, add the onion and cook for 3–4 mins until softened.
Turn the heat up to high, add the beef mince and cook for 3–4 mins, breaking it up with a wooden spoon until browned.
Pour in the sauce and let it bubble for 2–3 mins until thickened and sticky. Stir in the red chillies and cook for 1 more min.
Add the tenderstem to a heatproof bowl, cover and microwave for 2 mins until just tender.
Divide the rice between containers. Top with the sticky beef and broccoli, then finish with the spring onion greens. Box up and pop in the fridge until needed.

name: Spiced Green Chickpeas & Paneer
steps: Bring a large saucepan of water to the boil. Add the spinach and cook for 1-2 mins until wilted. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the spinach to a blender with some water from the pan and blitz until smooth.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Dice the paneer into 2cm cubes and finely chop the garlic.

Heat the oil in a pan over a medium heat. Add the mustard and cumin seeds and cook for about 30 seconds until fragrant and popping. Stir in the chopped garlic and cook for another 30 seconds until golden.
Pour in the spinach purée and tip in the chickpeas. Stir through the chilli powder, if using, and add the paneer. Bring everything to a gentle simmer for 3-4 mins. Pick the coriander.
Take the pan off the heat and leave to cool slightly. Then stir through the Greek yoghurt and season to taste with salt and black pepper.

To serve, spoon into Tupperware containers and top with coriander and a sprinkle of nigella seeds, if you fancy. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Chickpea & Tofu Tikka Masala
steps: Heat the grill to high.

Add half of the tikka paste to a bowl. Tear the tofu into chunky pieces and toss it through the paste. Season well with salt and pepper. Spread out on a foil-lined baking tray and slide under the grill for about 15 mins until golden and lightly charred.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion, garlic and ginger.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan set over a medium heat. Add the onion, garlic and ginger and cook for about 10 mins until soft and golden.
Stir in the remaining tikka paste and cook for a couple of minutes until fragrant.

Pour in the chopped tomatoes and coconut milk. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 10 mins. You can blitz the sauce smooth here with a stick blender if you want it silky or you can just leave it chunky.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas, then add them to the pan along with the grilled tofu. Simmer for another 5 mins to warm through.
Squeeze over the lemon juice, then serve up and scatter with fresh coriander leaves. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Chana Masala with Raita
steps: Peel and roughly chop the onion, garlic, and ginger. Remove the stems from the chillies. Blitz everything together in a blender until smooth to make a paste.
Heat the olive oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Add the paste and cook for 10 mins, stirring occasionally, until fragrant and slightly darkened.

Drain and rinse the chickpeas, then add them to the pan along with the chopped tomatoes. Bring to a simmer and cook for 15 mins until thickened. Stir through the garam masala and season with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, bring a pan of water to the boil and cook the eggs for 8 mins. Once done, cool them under cold water, peel, and halve.

For the raita, finely chop the mint. Halve the cucumber, scoop out the seeds, and grate or finely dice the flesh. Mix together the yoghurt, cucumber, mint, and the juice and zest of half a lemon. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Spoon the chana masala into Tupperware containers and store the raita in a separate container. Top each portion with a halved egg and scatter over some fresh coriander, if using. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch – they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Lentil & Halloumi Salad with Orange Dressing
steps: Heat grill to high. In a large bowl, whisk together the olive oil, red wine vinegar, and the juice of half the orange. Season with salt and pepper. Finely chop the shallot and add it to the bowl.
Drain and rinse the lentils, then tip them into the bowl with the shallot. Finely chop the parsley and dice the beetroot, then add both to the bowl. Toss to combine.
Slice the halloumi into thick pieces and place them on a tray lined with foil. Grill for 3–4 mins on each side until golden and crisp around the edges.
Add the grilled halloumi and rocket to the salad. Toss everything together until coated in the dressing, then taste and adjust the seasoning if needed.
Spoon your salad into your Tupperware containers. Box up and pop in the fridge, ready for when you need it. These keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Saag Tofu Lentils
steps: Preheat your oven to 180°C. Pat the tofu dry, then tear into pieces. Toss with half of the olive oil, a pinch of salt, and some pepper. Spread out on a baking tray and roast for 15 mins, until golden and crisp around the edges. Toss with the lime pickle.

While the tofu cooks, finely dice the onion, ginger and garlic. Heat the remaining olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion, garlic and ginger and cook for 5 mins until soft and starting to turn golden.

Stir in the curry powder. Cook for another 30 secs until fragrant. Add the lentils, stock cube, coconut milk, and water. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to the boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 20 mins, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender and creamy.
Stir through the spinach and cook for 2–3 mins until wilted.
Spoon into Tupperware containers, top with tofu and scatter with fresh coriander. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Dilly Rice Salad & Cottage Cheese
steps: Bring a saucepan of water to the boil. Lower in the eggs and boil for 8 mins. Drain and transfer to cold water to cool. Once cool enough to handle, peel and set aside.
Finely chop the shallot and add it to a large bowl with the zest and juice of the lemon. Season generously with salt and let it sit to mellow.
Microwave the rice pouch following pack instructions, or heat in a pan until piping hot.
Meanwhile, drain and rinse the lentils. Halve the cherry tomatoes. Halve the cucumber lengthways, scoop out the seeds and finely chop. Finely chop the dill.
Toss the hot rice into the lemony shallot bowl and mix well. Stir through the lentils, tomatoes, cucumber and dill. Taste and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper.
Halve the boiled eggs.

Spoon the salad into your Tupperware containers with a big dollop of cottage cheese on the side. Season the cottage cheese with salt and pepper, and top each with the halved egg. Box up and pop in the fridge, ready for when you need it. These keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Tofu Poke Bowl
steps: Dice the tofu into bite-sized chunks. Zest the lime. Add the tofu to a bowl along with the gochujang, soy sauce and lime zest. Toss to coat and set aside to marinate while you prep the rest.
Dice the mango into small pieces. If you'd prefer your quinoa warm, heat it now following pack instructions. Pick the coriander.
In a small bowl, mix the Greek yoghurt with the sriracha and lime juice. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.

Time to build your bowl. Divide the quinoa between Tupperware containers and top with the marinated tofu, mango, edamame and kimchi. Drizzle over the sriracha yoghurt and finish with a scattering of coriander and sesame seeds. Box up and pop in the fridge, ready for when you need it. These keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Creamy Roasted Pepper Chickpeas
steps: Finely slice the garlic. Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Roughly chop the roasted peppers and halve the cherry tomatoes.
Add the spinach to a colander in the sink and pour over two full kettles of boiling water until wilted. Set aside to drain.

Add the roasted peppers to a blender with the silken tofu, half the red chilli, and the juice of the lemon. Season generously with salt and pepper, then blitz until smooth. Finely slice the remaining chilli.

Heat a splash of the olive oil in a large pan over a medium-high heat. Add the cherry tomatoes and cook for 3–4 mins until just starting to soften. Add the remaining oil along with the garlic and smoked paprika, and cook for another 2 mins until fragrant.
Tip in the chickpeas and pour over the roasted pepper sauce. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 mins, then stir through the spinach until heated through. Taste and adjust the seasoning if needed.
Scatter with the sliced red chilli and fresh parsley. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Double Bean & Roasted Pepper Chilli
steps: Finely chop the onion and garlic, and slice the roasted peppers. Heat the olive oil in a large pan over a medium heat, then add the onion and garlic. Cook for 5 mins until softened and just turning golden.

Drain and rinse the beans, then add them to the pan along with the chipotle paste, oregano, and roasted peppers. Cook for 2 mins to let the flavours meld, then tip in the chopped tomatoes. Bring to a simmer and cook for 15 mins, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the spinach and cook for another 2 mins until just wilted.

Meanwhile, blitz the silken tofu in a blender until smooth. Season with salt and pepper, then zest in the lime and mix well. Stir half of the whipped tofu through the chilli, keeping the rest for serving.

Cut the lime into wedges. Serve the chilli in Tupperware containers, topped with the remaining whipped tofu, fresh coriander, and a squeeze of lime. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch - they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Baharat Chicken Bowl with Grated Feta
steps: Pop the feta into the freezer. This helps it grate more easily later.

Zest the lemons (reserve half for the tzatziki) and juice ¼ of the lemon into a bowl. Whisk together ¼ of the yoghurt with the baharat, lemon zest and juice. Season with salt. Cut the chicken into chunks, then toss in the marinade. Ideally chill overnight, or for at least 20 mins.
If you’re using bamboo skewers, soak them in water.

Peel and finely slice the red onion. Squeeze over the remaining lemon juice and season with salt and pepper. Scrunch together with your hands to help quick-pickle the onion. Cut the remaining lemon half into wedges for serving.

Cut the cucumber in half lengthwise and use a spoon to scoop out the seeds. Coarsely grate one-third of the cucumber and squeeze out the excess liquid. Chop most of the dill. Stir the grated cucumber, chopped dill and remaining lemon zest and yoghurt together to make a quick tzatziki. Season with salt and pepper.
Shred the lettuce. Chop the tomatoes and remaining cucumber into bite-sized chunks. Roughly chop the rest of the dill. Toss everything together with a drizzle of olive oil and season to taste.
Heat a grill pan on high. Thread the chicken onto skewers and grill for about 2 mins per side until lightly charred and cooked through.

Dish out the salad and top with pickled onions and a little drizzle of olive oil. Add the chicken skewers. Grate over the frozen feta and dollop on the tzatziki. Serve with lemon wedges and a pinch more baharat, if you fancy.

name: Tangy Tamarind Roasted Veg Salad
steps: Heat the oven to fan 200°C

Peel (optional) and chop the carrots & sweet potatoes into 2cm chunks. Toss with a drizzle of olive oil, season with salt & pepper, then spread out on a baking tray. Roast for 25–30 mins, until softened.
Meanwhile stir the ground cumin, tamarind purée & maple to make the sweet and tangy glaze. Taste & tweak the balance if needed, more tamarind for tang, more maple for sweetness. Set aside.

Trim and thinly slice the onion and green chilli. Pick the coriander leaves, set the coriander stems aside. Place the onion into a sieve and wash under cold running water. Then soak in a bowl full of ice water, this takes away the harsh bite and makes them last longer.
Chuck the coriander stems, yoghurt, green chillies, ground cumin & olive oil into a blender. Blitz until smooth, then season with salt, pepper & lemon juice to taste. Divide between boxes.
Once the veggies are cooked, pour the tamarind glaze over the top, toss together and return to the oven for 5-7 mins until sticky. Leave to cool before boxing up.
Drain the onions and toss with the sliced green chilli, coriander leaves and roasted veg.
Top the dressing with the grains and roasted veg mixture. Refrigerate until needed. Shake before serving.

name: Marry Me Chicken Pasta Bake
steps: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the pasta and cook until al dente, following pack instructions. Scoop out a mug of pasta water, then drain the pasta.
Meanwhile, slice the cherry tomatoes in half and tear the basil leaves.

Add the cottage cheese, sundried tomato paste, gochujang and garlic powder to a blender along with a splash of the reserved pasta water. Blend until smooth and creamy. Add more water as needed to loosen.

Tip the drained pasta into a large bowl along with the cooked chicken, halved cherry tomatoes and basil. Pour over the sauce and stir everything together until well coated. Add more pasta water if it looks a bit dry.

Transfer the pasta to an ovenproof dish, grate the Parmesan over the top and place under a hot grill for 5–10 mins until golden and bubbling on top. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch – they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Miso Chicken, Sesame Broccoli & Rice
steps: Start by mixing the miso paste, rice vinegar and sugar in a bowl. Rub the mixture all over the chicken breasts and set aside to marinate while you prep everything else.

Rinse the rice 2–3 times under cold water until it runs clear. Add to a lidded saucepan with the water and a pinch of salt. Set over a medium heat. Once simmering, pop the lid on, reduce the heat to low and cook for 10 mins. Turn off the heat and leave to steam for another 10 mins. Fluff with a fork.
Cut the broccoli into bite-sized florets and place in a heatproof bowl with a splash of water. Cover and microwave for 2½ mins until tender. Drain and toss with the soy sauce and sesame seeds.

Heat the butter and vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Once sizzling, add the chicken breasts and cook for 4 mins on one side. Flip and cook for another 4–5 mins until golden and cooked through. Turn off the heat and leave to rest in the pan for 3–4 mins.

Slice the chicken and plate everything up into Tupperware containers — fluffy rice, sesame broccoli and juicy miso chicken. Spoon over any buttery pan sauce and finish with a lemon wedge. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Chilli Garlic Prawn Rice Bowl With Cucumber Salad
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold water 2–3 times until the water runs clear. Tip into a lidded saucepan with the water and a pinch of salt. Set it over a medium heat. Once simmering, cover with a lid, reduce the heat to low and cook for 10 mins. Remove from the heat and leave covered for 10 mins. Fluff with a fork.
Meanwhile, finely slice the cucumber (use a mandoline if you have one) and add to a bowl with the rice vinegar, soy sauce and a pinch of salt. Mix well and set aside to lightly pickle.
Mince the garlic. Thinly slice the red chilli. Trim and finely slice the spring onion, keeping the whites and greens separate.
Place a frying pan over a medium heat and melt the butter. Add the garlic, spring onion whites and red chilli, then cook for 3 mins until softened and fragrant.

Add the prawns and cook for 90 seconds on each side until just pink. Stir through the sugar and sriracha, then toss for 2 more mins until thick and glossy. Turn off the heat and squeeze in the juice of one lime. Season to taste with salt.

Divide the rice between Tupperware containers. Top with the pickled cucumber and prawns. Finish with the spring onion greens, chopped coriander and lime wedges. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch — they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Sweet Potato, Minced Beef & Cottage Cheese Bowl
steps: Peel and dice the sweet potato into small chunks. Spray with oil and season with salt and pepper.
Cook in the air fryer at 200°C for 16–18 mins until golden and soft. Alternatively, roast in the oven at 180°C for 30 mins.
Meanwhile, set a non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the minced beef and cook for 6–7 mins until browned and cooked through. Stir in the taco seasoning and a pinch of salt.
While that’s cooking, halve the cherry tomatoes and shred the iceberg lettuce.

To plate or box up, spoon the roasted sweet potatoes, followed by the cottage cheese and taco beef. Add the lettuce, tomatoes and pickled onions. It will keep in the fridge for 3-4 days. Drizzle over the hot honey and finish with a pinch of chilli flakes if you like it spicy.

name: Creamy Spinach & Pea Orzo with Cod
steps: Finely chop the dill and parsley, reserving a few leaves for garnish. Peel and finely dice the shallots and garlic.
Set a large lidded frying pan over a medium heat with the olive oil. Once hot, add the shallots and garlic with a pinch of salt and cook for 3 mins until soft and translucent.
Tip in the orzo and stir to coat. Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 3 mins, stirring occasionally.
Add the spinach and peas to the pan and mix through until wilted, along with the chopped herbs.
Season the cod fillets with salt and pepper, then nestle them into the orzo. Cover with a lid and cook on low for 4–5 mins, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily and the orzo is al dente.
Squeeze over the juice of half a lemon and stir gently. Taste and season as needed.

Plate or box up the orzo and top with the cod. If eating later, store the yoghurt and herbs separately in an airtight container. If eating now, add a dollop of yoghurt, the reserved herbs and a lemon wedge. It will keep in the fridge for 3-4 days.

name: Minced Beef & Broccoli Stir Fry
steps: Mix all the sauce ingredients together in a bowl and set aside.
Mince the garlic and ginger. Cut the broccoli into bite-sized florets.
Place the broccoli in a heatproof bowl with the water. Cover and microwave for 3 mins until just tender. Drain and set aside. Alternatively, blanch it in boiling water for 2 mins.
Place a wok or large frying pan over a high heat with the vegetable oil. Once hot, add the beef mince and stir-fry for 3–4 mins until browned.
Add the ginger and garlic to the pan and cook for 2 mins until fragrant.
Tip in the broccoli and pour over the sauce. Toss everything together for 2–3 mins until the sauce thickens and coats the beef and veg.
Drizzle over the sesame oil and toss again. Remove from the heat.
Top with sesame seeds and extra white pepper if you fancy. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch – they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: One-Pot Thai Green Chicken Curry
steps: Slice the chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces. Trim the baby corn and mange tout. Finely slice the red chilli. Pick some coriander leaves for garnish and cut the lime into wedges.
Set a large saucepan over a medium heat. Pour in half the coconut milk and cook for 5 mins until the fat starts to split and it smells toasty.
Add the Thai Green Curry Paste and stir for another 5 mins until darker and super fragrant. Tip in the chicken and cook for 3–4 mins until just sealed.
Sprinkle in the sugar and let it bubble and caramelise for 2 mins. Pour in half the fish sauce and scrape up any sticky bits.
Add the rest of the coconut milk and the chicken stock. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 15 mins until slightly thickened and the chicken’s cooked through.
Chuck in the baby corn and mange tout for the final 2 mins. Stir through most of the coriander and the remaining fish sauce. Taste and season.
Serve over cooked rice and top with fresh chilli, crispy shallots, coriander leaves and a wedge of lime.

name: Quick Beef Chilli with Peppers and Onions
steps: Peel and dice the onion. Dice the red pepper. Peel and finely slice the garlic.

Set a large saucepan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the beef mince and fry for 5–6 mins, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until browned all over. Season well with salt and black pepper, then transfer to a plate.
In the same pan, heat another drizzle of oil if needed. Add the onion, pepper and garlic. Fry for 6–8 mins until soft and starting to catch.
Add the bay leaves, cayenne, cumin, oregano and smoked paprika. Stir and cook for 1–2 mins to toast the spices.
Squeeze in the tomato purée and stir for 2 mins until deepened in colour.

Pour in the chopped tomatoes and chicken stock, then return the browned beef to the pan. Give it all a good stir, bring to the boil, then reduce to a simmer for 25–30 mins until rich and thickened. Taste and season.
While that bubbles away, cook the rice according to pack instructions if you haven’t already. Grate the Cheddar and cut the lime into wedges.
Spoon the chilli over bowls of rice. Top with sour cream, grated Cheddar, a few coriander leaves and a wedge of lime. Finish with black pepper.

name: Chipotle Chicken with Lemony Kale Rice
steps: Heat your oven grill to high.
Cut the chicken thighs into quarters. Peel and finely slice the onions. Peel and grate the garlic.
