Chuck the chicken, onions, chipotle paste, garlic, oregano, cumin, olive oil, salt and pepper into a large bowl. Toss until everything is coated.

Spread the chicken mix onto a baking tray in an even layer. Slide under the grill on the top shelf and cook for 15–20 mins, turning halfway, until the chicken is cooked through and starting to char at the edges.
While the chicken cooks, peel and finely chop the remaining garlic. Melt the butter in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and fry for 1 min until fragrant.
Add the kale and cook for 2–3 mins until starting to wilt. Stir in the rice, water, a good pinch of salt and the zest of half the lemon.

Bring to the boil, cover with a lid and turn the heat down to low. Cook for 12 mins, then remove from the heat and leave to steam, covered, for 5 mins. Fluff up the rice with a fork and squeeze over the juice of the lemon.
Serve the chipotle chicken over the rice with a wedge of lime, some grated Cheddar and a big dollop of yoghurt.

name: Harissa Chicken Traybake with Herby Grains
steps: Heat the oven grill to high.
Cut the chicken thighs into quarters. Peel and finely slice the onions. Grate the garlic.
Add the chicken, onions, harissa and grated garlic to a large bowl. Drizzle in some olive oil, season with salt and black pepper, and toss to coat.

Tip everything onto a baking tray and spread into an even layer. Slide under the grill on the top shelf and cook for 15–20 mins, turning halfway, until the chicken is cooked through and the edges are starting to catch.
While that grills, dice the courgette. Finely chop the dill and parsley.
Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Chuck in the courgette and fry for 6–8 mins until golden and soft, seasoning as you go.
Tip in the grains and stir through until hot. Take off the heat, then stir through the herbs and squeeze in the juice of half a lemon. Taste and tweak the seasoning if it needs it.
Serve the grilled chicken and onions over the herby grains with a big spoonful of Skyr yoghurt on the side.

name: Chicken & Basil Stir Fry
steps: Start by making the sauce. Add the oyster sauce, soy, fish sauce and sugar to a bowl. Mix until the sugar dissolves, then set aside.
Finely slice the shallots and chilli, and mince the garlic. Then roughly chop the tenderstem broccoli.
Set a large wok or frying pan over a medium heat and drizzle in the oil. Add the garlic, shallots and chilli, and stir-fry for 2–3 mins until fragrant.

Add the chicken mince and cook for 5-8 mins until golden, breaking it up with a spoon as you go (If you're making a bigger portion it's best to do this in batches, to allow the mince to fry properly). Pour in the sauce and let it bubble away for another 2 mins until sticky.

Tip in the broccoli and pour in the water. Cook for 3–4 mins until the beans are tender and most of the liquid has reduced. Add the basil and stir through to wilt. Finish by squeezing in the juice of half the limes.
For the eggs, either boil for 7 mins, then peel and store in the fridge, or fry them fresh when you’re ready to eat.

To portion, divide the cooked rice between four containers, then top with the chicken mince. This’ll keep in the fridge for up to 4 days. And serve with the remaining lime. Reheat until piping hot before serving.

name: Cherry Tomato & Cottage Cheese Pasta Salad
steps: If your pasta isn’t already cooked, bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and cook the fusilli following pack instructions. Drain, rinse under cold water and set aside to cool.

Halve the cherry tomatoes and finely slice the courgette. Grate the Parmesan. Toast the pine nuts in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 2–3 mins until golden. Tear the basil leaves. Shred or dice the cooked chicken.

Tip the cooled pasta into a large mixing bowl. Add the cherry tomatoes, sundried tomato paste, cottage cheese, chicken, courgette and most of the basil. Season generously with salt and black pepper, then toss everything together until well combined.
Divide between bowls or containers. Finish with the toasted pine nuts, a scattering of Parmesan and the rest of the basil.

name: Spiced Spinach, Chickpea & Halloumi Curry
steps: Dice the halloumi into 1.5cm cubes. Set a large deep frying pan over medium-high heat and dry-fry the halloumi for 3–4 mins until golden on most sides. Remove from the pan and set aside — no need to clean the pan.
Add the ghee or butter to the same pan. Finely chop the onion and fry for 3–4 mins until soft and turning golden at the edges.
Mince the garlic, grate or mince the ginger, and finely chop the green chilli (if using). Add to the pan and cook for 1 min, stirring constantly.
Add the curry powder and half of the garam masala. Stir for 30 seconds until everything smells amazing.
Add the spinach to the pan — all at once if frozen, or in batches if fresh. Cook for 8–10 mins, stirring often, until wilted and most of the moisture has cooked off.

Stir through the chickpeas and cook for 1–2 mins. Take the pan off the heat and leave to cool slightly. Spoon in the yoghurt and gently stir through — off the heat to stop it splitting. Season well with salt and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Return the halloumi to the pan and gently warm through. Sprinkle over the remaining garam masala.
Serve over cooked rice with some fresh coriander and a few slices of red chilli on top.

name: Kale & Cottage Cheese Caesar Salad
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan. Tear the sourdough into bite-sized pieces and tip onto a baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt, and toss to coat. Roast for 15–20 mins until golden and crisp, then set aside to cool.
Spread the Tenderstem out on a separate tray, drizzle with a little oil and a pinch of salt, and roast for 10–12 mins until lightly charred.
Zest the lemon, then halve and juice it.

To make the dressing, add the cottage cheese, anchovies, Parmesan, garlic and Worcestershire sauce to a blender with a splash of water. Blitz until smooth, then season to taste with salt, black pepper and lemon juice.
Shred the kale into a large bowl, sprinkle with a pinch of salt and scrunch it with your hands for a minute or so until softened.
Add the kale, cooked chicken, roasted broccoli and croutons to a large bowl. Pour over the dressing and toss until everything’s well coated.
Serve with extra Parmesan, a wedge of lemon and a crack of black pepper.

name: Honey Za’atar Halloumi, Herby Pomegranate Slaw & Hummus
steps: Slice the cabbage in half lengthways and finely shred. Thinly slice the red onion. Roughly chop three-quarters of the dill. Add everything to a large bowl.

Drizzle over the pomegranate molasses, squeeze in the juice of half a lemon, and add the olive oil. Season with salt and pepper, then mix well to combine. Let the slaw sit and lightly pickle while you cook the halloumi.

Cut the halloumi into 2cm cubes. Set a frying pan over medium-high heat (no oil needed). Fry the halloumi cubes for 1–2 mins on each side until golden and crisp. Drizzle in the honey and sprinkle over the za’atar. Cook for 30 seconds, tossing to coat, then take off the heat.
Divide the hummus between two containers or plates. Spoon over the herby slaw, top with the sticky halloumi and finish with the remaining dill.

name: Chipotle Roast Corn, Marinated Feta & Wild Rice Salad
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Drain the sweetcorn really well, then spread it out on a baking tray. Drizzle over half of the olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and roast for 15–20 mins, tossing halfway, until golden and crisp at the edges.

Toast the cumin seeds in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 1–2 mins until fragrant, then tip into a bowl. Crumble in the feta into big bite-sized chunks. Zest and juice in one of the limes, add the remaining olive oil, and stir gently. Set aside to marinate at room temperature while the corn roasts.

Heat the rice pouch according to pack instructions. Tip into a large bowl, season with salt and pepper, then zest and juice in the second lime. Stir through the chipotle paste and baby spinach while the rice is still warm to help it wilt slightly.
Divide the chipotle rice between containers or bowls. Top with the roasted corn, marinated feta and a scattering of fresh coriander.

name: Bombay Cauliflower & Turmeric Rice with Tamarind Yoghurt
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan.

Cut the cauliflower into bite-sized florets and tip into a large roasting tin. Toss with half of the turmeric, plus all of the cumin and coriander with a drizzle of olive oil and a big pinch of salt. Roast for 25–30 mins until golden and tender.
Meanwhile, peel and finely slice the garlic.
Place a medium saucepan over a medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Fry the garlic for 1 min, then stir through the rice and remaining turmeric until coated.
Pour in the stock, bring to the boil, then cover with a lid. Reduce the heat to low and cook for 10–12 mins until the liquid has been absorbed and the rice is fluffy.
While the rice and cauliflower cook, mix the yoghurt, tamarind paste and honey in a small bowl until smooth.
Slice the cucumber into thin half-moons and roughly chop the coriander.
Pack the rice into lunchboxes, top with the roasted cauliflower, spoon over the tamarind yoghurt and finish with cucumber and coriander.

name: High-Protein Cauliflower Mac & Cheese
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil.
Cut the cauliflower into florets, toss with olive oil, salt, and pepper, then roast for 15 mins until just tender and golden. Grate the cheeses.
Add the pasta to the boiling salted water and cook according to the packet instructions. Drain, reserving a little of the pasta water.
In a blender, combine the silken tofu, Dijon mustard, garlic powder, parmesan, and a pinch of nutmeg. Season well with salt and pepper, then blend until smooth and creamy.

Return the pasta and roasted cauliflower to the pan. Pour over the tofu sauce and stir to coat. Add most of the cheeses (saving a handful for the top) and heat gently for a couple of minutes until the cheese has melted, loosening with a splash of pasta water if needed.
Transfer to an ovenproof dish, sprinkle with the remaining cheese, and bake for 10 mins until golden and bubbling. Finely chop the parsley.

Serve the pasta bake into a Tupperware container topped with chopped parsley and a crack of black pepper. Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch – they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Chicken & Egg Fried Rice
steps: Mix all the sauce ingredients together in a small bowl.
Chop the chicken into bite-sized pieces, peel and finely mince the garlic. Trim and slice the spring onions, keeping the whites and greens separate. Crack the eggs into a bowl and beat.
Heat a large wok or frying pan over a high heat with the vegetable oil. Once hot, add the chicken and stir-fry for 4–6 mins until golden and cooked through. Transfer to a plate and set aside.

In the same pan, add the garlic and the whites of the spring onions. Cook for 1–2 mins until softened and fragrant. Push everything to one side of the pan and pour in the beaten eggs. Let them set slightly, then break them apart and stir through.
Add the day-old rice to the pan. Spread it out evenly and leave it for 1–2 mins to catch some colour, then toss well to break up any clumps.
Return the chicken to the pan and pour in the rest of the sauce directly onto the hot surface. Toss everything together until evenly coated and the rice is piping hot.
Stir through the frozen peas and beansprouts and cook for 1–2 mins until just heated through.

Divide the fried rice between containers and top with and a handful of the sliced green spring onions. Leave to cool and box up and pop in the fridge until needed. You can reheat in the wok or the microwave or enjoy cold.

name: Thai Red Curry Salmon with Lime & Coconut Rice
steps: Zest both limes onto a small plate and set aside.
In a bowl, mix the Thai red curry paste, honey and the juice of both limes with 50ml of water. Season lightly with salt and pepper.

Wash the rice thoroughly in cold water, then drain really well. Tip into a small saucepan and pour in the coconut milk. Add the lime zest and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to low, cover with a lid and cook for 5 mins. Lay the trimmed green beans on top, cover again and cook for another 5 mins. Turn off the heat and let everything steam for a few more minutes with the lid on.
Cut the salmon into chunky, bite-sized pieces and season with salt.

Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the salmon pieces and fry for 1 min on each side until golden. Turn the heat to low and pour in the curry dressing. Let it bubble away until thickened and sticky, coating the salmon.
Fluff the coconut and lime rice with a fork and divide between bowls or containers. Add the green beans, top with the sticky salmon bites and scatter over the coriander.

name: Buffalo Chicken, Celery & Blue Cheese Grain Bowl
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C. Add the chicken thighs to a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil. Sprinkle over the smoked paprika, garlic granules, brown sugar, salt and pepper. Drizzle with a bit more oil and spread into an even layer, skin-side up. Roast for 45 mins until cooked through and golden crisp.
Drizzle your hot sauce (we used Frank's Red Hot Sauce) over the cooked chicken and return to the oven for 5 more mins. Set aside to rest while you prep everything else.

Finely dice the celery and add to a large bowl. Crumble the blue cheese into bite-sized chunks and add to the bowl. Heat the grain pouches according to pack instructions, then tip the grains into the same bowl.
Add the natural yoghurt, apple cider vinegar and garlic granules. Season with salt and pepper, then mix well. Tear in most of the dill and gently fold through.
Divide the grain salad between containers or bowls and top each with 2 buffalo chicken thighs. Finish with the remaining dill and a little extra drizzle of hot sauce, if you like.

name: Cherry Tomato, Spring Onion & Tabasco Pasta Salad
steps: Cook the rigatoni according to pack instructions. Drain well, reserving a mug of the pasta cooking water.
Finely dice the cherry tomatoes and tip into a large bowl. Finely slice the spring onions and add to the same bowl.

Splash in the olive oil and red wine vinegar, then season generously with salt and pepper. Add a few good dashes of Tabasco and stir to combine. Taste and adjust the heat to your liking — the pasta will mellow the flavours a bit.
Tip the drained pasta into the tomato bowl and toss everything together really well. Leave to cool for around 20 mins, tossing every now and then to help the pasta absorb the dressing.
Once the pasta has cooled, toss through the rocket. Season again if needed, then portion into containers and store in the fridge until ready to eat.

name: Ponzu Noodles With Hot Smoked Salmon
steps: Cook the udon noodles following pack instructions. Drain and refresh under cold water, then dunk into a bowl of iced water to chill. Set aside.

Peel and finely julienne or grate the ginger. Dissolve the dashi powder in a splash of hot water in a jug, then top up with cold water. Stir in the soy sauce, rice vinegar and ginger. Add a few ice cubes to chill the broth.
Drain the tofu and gently pat dry with kitchen paper. Cut into 2cm cubes.
Divide the noodles between bowls and pour over the cold ponzu-style broth. Flake the hot smoked salmon over the top, then add the tofu cubes.
Top with a spoonful of kimchi, sliced spring onions and a sprinkle of shichimi togarashi or chilli flakes. Finish with toasted sesame seeds, if you like.

name: Sweet & Sticky Chicken with Broccoli Rice
steps: Finely slice the garlic and roughly chop the broccoli.
Add the butter to a large saucepan set over a medium heat. Once melted, add the garlic and cook for 2 mins, stirring regularly until softened. Add the chopped broccoli and cook for another 2–3 mins.

Wash the rice and stir it through the broccoli mix. Pour in the water and bring to the boil. Pop a lid on, reduce the heat to low and cook for 12 mins. Turn off the heat and leave covered for 10 mins to finish steaming.
Meanwhile, mix the oyster sauce, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sriracha and honey in a small bowl.

Slice the chicken thighs into bite-sized chunks — about 5–6 pieces per thigh. Set a large frying pan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the chicken in a single layer (you may need to work in batches to avoid overcrowding). Season with salt and cook for 6 mins until golden and crispy on one side. Flip and cook for another 2–3 mins until cooked through.
Take the pan off the heat and pour in the sauce. Toss to coat the chicken in the glaze. If the sauce looks too runny, return to the heat for 1–2 mins to thicken slightly.

Thinly slice the spring onions. Spoon the broccoli rice into bowls or containers, top with the sticky chicken and any sauce left in the pan. Finish with spring onions, sesame seeds and a wedge of lemon.

name: Chicken Satay Grain Bowl
steps: Zest and juice the lime into a bowl. Add the soy sauce, a pinch of salt and 1 tsp of black pepper. Stir to combine, then add the chicken thighs and toss to coat. Set aside to marinate while you prep the rest.

Set a heavy-bottomed frying pan over a medium-high heat. Once hot, lay the chicken thighs into the pan and cook for 10 mins on one side without moving. Flip and cook for another 4–5 mins until nicely golden and cooked through. Set aside to rest.

For the satay sauce, mix the peanut butter, sriracha, soy sauce, lime juice, honey and water in a bowl until smooth. If it’s too thick, loosen with another splash of water. Taste and adjust — you want a good balance of zing and heat.

Strip the kale into a large mixing bowl, then add a good pinch of salt and a drizzle of olive oil. Massage with your hands for about a minute until softened. Drain the butter beans and stir them through. Heat the grains following pack instructions and tip into the bowl.
Trim and thinly slice the spring onions, separating the whites and greens. Add the whites to the bowl with a splash of the dressing and toss to combine.
Slice the rested chicken.

Divide the kale and grain salad between bowls or containers. Top with the sliced chicken, drizzle over the remaining dressing and finish with the spring onion greens, sliced chilli (if using) and a lime wedge for squeezing.

name: Mexican Dense Bean Salad
steps: Drain and rinse the black beans and kidney beans. Drain the sweetcorn. Drain and slice the roasted peppers.
Peel and finely slice the red onion. Add it to a small bowl with the juice of one lime and a pinch of salt. Massage and set aside.
Halve the cherry tomatoes. Peel, pit and dice the avocados. Add the beans, sweetcorn, peppers, tomatoes and avocado to a large mixing bowl.

Add the silken tofu to a high-speed blender with most of the coriander, the juice of the remaining two limes and the jalapeños (seeds removed if you’re not into spice). Grate in the garlic, add the tahini and season generously with salt and pepper. Blitz until smooth.
Pour the dressing over the bean mixture, then add the pickled onions. Toss well to coat everything, taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

Scatter with the remaining coriander and serve. If making ahead box up for later and chill until needed. 
The salad will keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Antipasti Dense Bean Salad
steps: Drain and rinse the butter beans. Drain the artichokes and roughly chop them. Drain and chop the pickled peppers. Drain and chop the sundried tomatoes. Drain the mozzarella. Dice the salami. Zest the lemon and set aside.
Bring a pot of salted water to the boil. Add the green beans and cook for 1 min, then drain and cool under cold water. Drain again and set aside.
Grab a large mixing bowl. Squeeze in the lemon juice and finely grate in the garlic. Add the olive oil, balsamic vinegar and honey, then whisk until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.

Add the butter beans, artichokes, pickled peppers, mozzarella, sundried tomatoes, salami and green beans to the bowl. Add in the lemon zest. Give everything a good mix, taste and adjust seasoning. If making ahead, share between Tupperware containers and chill until needed.
The salad will last for up to 3 days in the fridge.

name: Greek Dense Bean Salad
steps: Drain and rinse the kidney beans, chickpeas and butter beans. Dice the tomatoes into irregular chunks. Slice the cucumber in half lengthways, scoop out the seeds and chop. Remove the seeds from the pepper and chop into bite-sized chunks. Peel and finely slice the shallot. Pit the olives, if needed.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the olive oil, red wine vinegar and dried oregano. Add the sliced shallot and let it sit for a few minutes.

Tip in the chopped pepper, tomato, cucumber, beans and olives. Dice the feta and chuck it on top. Season with salt and pepper, then give everything a good mix before serving.
If making ahead, box up and chill until needed. The salad will last for up to 3 days in the fridge.

name: Spicy Miso Dense Bean Salad
steps: Bring a pot of salted water to the boil. Add the edamame beans and boil for 5 mins, then drain and rinse under cold water. Drain and rinse the cannellini beans.
Slice the romaine lettuce. Halve the cucumber lengthways, scoop out the seeds and slice. Finely slice the spring onions.
In a large bowl, whisk together the white miso, gochujang, maple syrup and rice vinegar until smooth.
Add the cannellini beans, edamame, quinoa, lettuce, cucumber and spring onions. Toss everything together and season with salt to taste.

Top with the toasted sesame seeds and torn coriander leaves before serving.If making ahead, box up and chill until needed. The salad will keep for up to 3 days in the fridge. Store the dressing separately to keep the salad fresh.

name: High Protein Chopped Broccoli Salad
steps:
Rinse the quinoa very well and add to a saucepan. Cover the quinoa with double the amount of water and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil and then reduce the heat and simmer for 12 mins. 
Drain and rinse under cold water in a colander. Set aside or in the fridge to cool while you prepare the rest.
Finely chop the broccoli florets. Peel the tough skin from the broccoli stem and finely chop the broccoli stem or grate it on a cheesegrater. Add to a large bowl.
Drain the chickpeas, finely chop the red onion and add these to the bowl. Add the dried cranberries, sunflower seeds and peanuts to the bowl.
To make the dressing, mix all of the ingredients in a jar and shake well to combine.

Toss the salad with the dressing, before dividing between containers. Don't worry about it getting soggy, the salad will stay crunchy and soak up all dressing as well. Box up and pop in the fridge, ready to grab and go!
These keep for up to 3 days in the fridge.

name: Turmeric Cauliflower & Halloumi Rice Bowl
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C. Cut the cauliflower into rough florets and add to a large roasting tray. Cut the halloumi into chunky cubes and add to the tray. Peel the onions and cut into chunky wedges, then add to the tray along with the whole garlic cloves, still in their skins. Add the spices and olive oil, toss well, then season well. Slide into the oven and bake for 30 mins.
Cook the rice following pack instructions and tip into a bowl. Finely chop most of the coriander and add to the rice along with the juice of the lemon.
Remove the tray from the oven, fish out the garlic cloves and carefully squeeze the squishy garlic out of their skins into the rice. Season with plenty of salt and pepper.

Spoon the rice into your Tupperware containers and top with the spiced veggies. Drizzle with chilli oil, scatter with the remaining coriander leaves and finish with sesame seeds. 
Once they've cooled down a bit, box them up and pop in the fridge, until needed - they'll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Air-Fryer Negima Yakitori
steps: Cut your spring onions and chicken thighs into roughly 2cm-sized pieces.
Thread the chicken and spring onion pieces tightly onto skewers, alternating between them. Season with salt and white pepper and set aside.
In a small saucepan, combine the soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, and mirin. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce to a simmer and cook for around 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Toss the Padrón peppers with olive oil and salt.
Preheat the air fryer to 200°C. Add the skewers, brush with some glaze, and drizzle with a little olive oil. Cook for 9-10 minutes, brushing with more glaze halfway through.
Add the Padron peppers to the air fryer, brush the chicken again with glaze, and cook for another 5-6 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the peppers are charred.
Cook the rice according to package instructions, adding the edamame 5 minutes before the end of the cooking time.

Spoon the edamame rice into your lunch boxes, then top with the skewers and Padrón peppers. Dust with shichimi togarashi, if using.
Leave to stand for a bit and once cooled, box up and stash in the fridge until you need them - they'll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Sticky Honey & Miso Aubergine Rice Bowl
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan.

Cut the aubergines into wedges and place them on a baking tray. In a bowl, mix the honey, miso, water, sesame oil and lemon juice, then pour over the aubergines, tossing to coat. Roast for 30-35 mins until soft and sticky. Once cooked, remove from the oven and drizzle over the pomegranate molasses.
Meanwhile, cook the rice following pack instructions. Four mins before the end of the cooking time, add the green beans. Slice the red chilli and pick the parsley leaves.

Divide the rice between bowls or meal prep containers. Top with the sticky aubergines, drizzling over any leftover marinade from the tray. Scatter with sesame seeds, red chilli and parsley. Finish with pomegranate seeds, if using. It will keep well in the fridge for 3 days.

name: Dense Bean Salad with Tomato & Basil Vinaigrette
steps: Drain and rinse the beans, then add them to a large salad bowl.

To a blender, add the tomatoes, shallot, garlic, olive oil, Dijon mustard and red wine vinegar. Season with salt and black pepper, then blitz until smooth. For a finer dressing, strain through a sieve and discard any pulp.
Tear the basil into pieces then add to the beans along with the rocket. Season with salt and pepper then toss to combine.

Plate or box up the beans then tear over the mozzarella. If eating later, store the dressing separately in an airtight container. If eating now, drizzle the dressing over the top. It will keep in the fridge for 3-4 days.

name: Courgette Butter Bean Pasta Salad
steps: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and cook the orecchiette or your chosen pasta according to the package instructions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water to cool it down quickly. Set aside.
Tip the pumpkin seeds into a small frying pan over a medium high heat, toast for 2-3 mins, tossing regularly, until they start to pop. Tip onto a plate to cool a little.
Slice the courgettes into thin rounds or half-moons. No need to cook them, they’re delicious raw! Pit and halve the green olives, if not already pitted. Rinse and drain the butter beans.
Make the dressing. In a small bowl or jug, whisk together the pesto, olive oil, and the juice of the lemon. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, add the cooked pasta, raw courgettes, green olives, butter beans, and toasted pumpkin seeds. Shave the Parmesan and add to the bowl along with the mint leaves.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss everything together until well combined.

Divide the pasta salad between your Tupperware containers with the remaining toasted pumpkin seeds and Parmesan cheese grated over the top.
Once at room temp, box up and pop in the fridge ready to grab for lunch - they'll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Crispy Tofu Noodle Salad with Wasabi Vinaigrette
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Line a baking tray with baking parchment.

Dice the tofu into 2cm pieces. Mix the cornflour, curry powder, and a pinch of salt in a tray, then toss the tofu in the mix to coat evenly. Spread onto the tray, drizzle with sesame oil, and roast for 20-25 mins until crisp and golden.
Cook the noodles following pack instructions, then drain and rinse under cold water. Toss in a large bowl with ⅓ of the sesame oil to prevent sticking.
Cut the mange tout in half. Shred the romaine and roughly chop the coriander. Add to the noodles and toss to combine. Thinly slice the radishes and set aside.

In a bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, light brown sugar, rice vinegar, wasabi paste, and remaining sesame oil. Finely grate in the garlic and whisk until emulsified. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

Box up the noodle salad and top with the crispy tofu, radishes and sesame seeds. If eating later, store the dressing separately in an airtight container. If eating now, drizzle the dressing over the top. Everything will keep well in the fridge for 3 days.

name: Juicy Chipotle Pineapple Chicken & Rice
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Add the chipotle and cumin to a baking tray. Grate the garlic in, season generously with salt and mix together. Toss the chicken through the marinade with a drizzle of olive oil. Arrange the chicken and bake for 15-20 mins until fully cooked.

Meanwhile, trim and slice the pineapple into 2cm chunks. Thinly slice the onion. Put the onion slices into a bowl and squeeze the juice of 1 lime over them. Season with salt and set aside to pickle. Pick half the coriander leaves and finely mince the rest. Dice the avocado into even-sized cubes.
Once the chicken is cooked, add the pineapple to the tray, switch the oven setting to grill and cook until the pineapple and chicken start to char.
Reheat the rice and stir the minced coriander and zest of half a lime through. Season with salt.

Divide the rice between Tupperware containers, then top with the chicken and pineapple, avocado, pickled onions, store-bought tomatillo salsa and remaining coriander leaves. Box up and pop in the fridge ready to grab and go (they'll keep for up to 3 days).

name: Apple Green Goddess With Herby Dressing
steps: Add the herbs, crème fraîche, peeled garlic, olive oil, Dijon and ½ the lime to a blender, then season with salt and pepper. Blitz until smooth, then taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Slice the apple into matchsticks, then the sugar snaps into 2cm pieces on a diagonal.
Cook the edamame in boiling water for 7 mins then drain.
Using a veg peeler, finely shred the green cabbage and peel, pit and slice the avocado.
Squeeze the rest of the lime juice into a bowl with the cabbage, seasoning with salt. Massage until it just starts to soften. Then add the edamame, sugar snaps, drained beans and apple mixing well.
Box up the slaw. If eating immediately, drizzle with the dressing. If not, box the dressing up for later.

name: Spanakopita Orzo
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C. Tip the pine nuts onto a baking tray and roast for 10-12 mins until golden.

Finely slice the onion and chop the garlic. Heat a splash of oil in the biggest pot you have, then add the onion and fry for 10 mins over a medium heat. Add the garlic, cook for another 2 mins and pour in the wine, cooking off until evaporated.

Add a big handful of spinach and rocket – it will take a few goes to get it all wilted down. Keep wilting and adding the leaves until it’s all used up, then remove the mixture from the pan and set aside to cool.

Tip the orzo into the pan along with the vegetable stock. Give it a mix once its added to the pot to prevent sticking, bring it up to a simmer, cover with a lid and cook for 10 mins until the liquid has been absorbed.

Meanwhile, squeeze as much of the liquid out of the spinach mix as you can, then finely chop. Finely chop the dill and mix most of it through the orzo, along with the chopped spinach. Grate in the zest of the lemon with a squeeze of the juice, then season with salt and pepper.
Spoon out the orzo into your Tupperware containers. Once cool, top with crumbled feta, the pine nuts and the remaining dill.Box up and pop in the fridge - they'll last for up to 3 days.

name: Coconutty Air Fryer Tofu & Quinoa Salad with Peanut Dressing
steps: Tip the desiccated coconut into one bowl or tray, ⅗ of the coconut cream into another, and the cornflour into a third. Season each one with salt and pepper.

Cut the tofu into 3cm cubes. Dredge in the cornflour, coating all the sides. Dunk in the coconut cream and shake off the excess before tossing in the desiccated coconut, pressing down firmly to make it really stick. Set aside on a tray.

Add the tofu to the air fryer then drizzle with oil. Heat the air fryer to 180°C and cook for 15 mins, then flip and cook for a further 10 mins until evenly golden. Carefully remove from the basket and set aside.
Cut the Tenderstem into thirds and toss with olive oil, salt and pepper. Add to the air fryer basket and cook at 180°C for 8 mins. Add the tofu back in and cook for 2 mins until warmed through.
For the peanut dressing mix the peanut butter with the remaining coconut cream, juice of ½ the lime, the sesame oil and the soy sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Finely chop half of the mint and mix with the quinoa and the remaining lime juice.

Spoon out the quinoa between your Tupperware containers, top each with the broccoli and tofu and then garnish with mint and a pinch of chilli flakes, if you're feeling fancy. Box up and pop in the fridge - these will keep for up to 3 days.Keep the peanut dressing separate – either pour a little over in the morning or stash it in a little pot inside your lunch box to add just before eating.

name: Everything Salmon Rice Bowl
steps: Heat your oven to 190°C. Place a small baking tray in there to preheat.
Mix your poppy seeds, sesame seeds, garlic powder, onion powder and salt in a bowl. Give it all a mix.

Prep your salad. Smack your baby cucumbers with the side of a knife, then cut them into small chunks. Get them in a sieve set over a bowl, and sprinkle over a little salt. Leave them to sit whilst you prep the rest.

Finely slice your pickles and your spring onions. Finely chop your dill too. Get these in a bowl with your rice and quinoa, and your salted cucumber. Crumble in your feta and give it a good mix. Season with the juice of ½ your lemon and a little salt.
Pat your salmon fillets dry, and place them on a board skin side down. Press your everything seasoning mix all over the salmon flesh (avoiding the skin).
Remove your hot baking sheet from the oven, and place a piece of baking parchment on it. Pop your salmon fillets skin side down on top, then drizzle on a little olive oil, and bake them for 7 mins.
Turn your grill up to high. Blast your salmon under the grill for 2 mins until the top has turned a little golden.

Spoon your salad into your Tupperware containers, then top with your salmon, a dollop of soured yoghurt and nestle in a little wedge of lemon. Box up and pop in the fridge ready for your when you need it. These keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Crispy Chicken, Brown Rice, Chickpeas & Tzatziki
steps: Place the chicken thighs skin-side down on a chopping board. Run a knife along each side of the bone to expose the bone. Using scissors, cut underneath the bone to remove it. Repeat with the remaining chicken thighs.
Cut the courgette in half lengthways and then into half moons. Cut the red onion into large chunks.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper and add skin side down into a cold, large frying pan and set it over a medium heat. Cook for 10-15 mins until the chicken skin is golden brown.

While the chicken is cooking, make the tzatziki. Grate the cucumber into a bowl and season with salt. Set aside for 5 mins then squeeze out the excess water. Meanwhile, chop the dill then add to the squeezed cucumber along with the yoghurt, the zest of the lemon and the juice of ½ the lemon. Grate in the garlic. Mix well to combine then season to taste with salt. Set aside.
When the chicken skin is golden brown and crispy, flip the chicken thighs and cook for a further 2 mins. Remove them from the pan and set aside.

Add the red onion, courgette and spices to the pan. Grate in the garlic then cook over a medium heat until soft. (If anything catches on the bottom of the pan, just add a little water and scrape it up). Add the drained chickpeas and cooked rice to the pan. Cook over a medium heat for 2-3 mins until everything has come together. Season with salt, pepper and MSG.
Meanwhile, pick the parsley leaves and cut the chicken into thick slices.
To serve, divide the rice between Tupperware containers then top with the chicken and tzatziki. Sprinkle over the parsley and finish with a lemon wedge. Pop in the fridge until needed.

name: Greek(ish) Tomato & Olive Barley
steps: Rinse the pearl barley. Finely slice the garlic. Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a pan over a medium heat and fry the garlic for 2 mins. Add the tomato purée, fennel seeds and cinnamon and cook for 1 min. Add the canned tomatoes, barley and stock, season with salt and pepper, bring to the boil then simmer for 45 mins, stirring often to prevent it from sticking to the bottom.

Heat the grill and grill the broccoli for 8 mins, turning halfway. Meanwhile, finely slice the red onion and tip it into a bowl with the lemon juice. Tear the olives in half, chop the dill and add both to the bowl along with the broccoli. Give it a mix and season with salt and pepper.

Divide the barley between your Tupperware containers and top with your broccoli and olive mix. Once they've cooled a bit, box up and pop in the fridge.
These will keep for up to 3 days in the fridge.

name: Saucy Tomatoey Gochujang Noodles with Smoked Tofu
steps: Finely slice the cucumber and add it to a bowl with the chilli oil, rice vinegar, a pinch of salt and the sesame seeds. Finely slice the spring onions and set aside for garnish.

Cut the smoked tofu cut into 2cm pieces. Set a frying pan over a medium heat with a splash of oil. Once hot, add the tofu, cooking on all sides until golden. Then add in the soy sauce and maple syrup, let it bubble away until it gets nice and sticky and then take off the heat. Set aside.

Heat a splash of olive oil in a large pan over a medium heat. Grate in the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 mins. Add the tomato purée and cook for another 2 mins, then remove from the heat. Add the cooked mixture to a blender with the silken tofu and gochujang. Blitz until smooth, seasoning with salt and pepper to taste. Return this sauce mixture to the pan.
Cook the noodles following the pack instructions, then drain, reserving some of the cooking water. Toss the noodles through the sauce, loosening with a splash of the reserved cooking water if needed.

Dish out the noodles between Tupperware containers. Top each with the cucumber salad and crispy tofu, a drizzle of crispy chilli oil and a sprinkling of spring onions.
Box up and pop in the fridge - these will keep for up to 3 days.

name: Chicken & Garlic Rice with Crunchy Slaw
steps: Preheat the oven to fan 180°C. Bash the garlic, trim and thinly slice the ginger and spring onions. Wash the rice until the water runs clear.
Add the soy sauce, honey, 5-spice and bashed garlic into a bowl. Mix the chicken thighs through until coated.

Place an oven-proof frying pan over medium heat with a drizzle of oil (if you don’t have one you can transfer the dish into a baking tray before roasting). Once hot, add the chicken, and sear on one side (keep the chicken marinade). Transfer to a plate.

Add the spring onions whites and ¾ of the greens along with the ginger into the empty pan. Stir-fry until softened and fragrant, 1-2 mins. Tip the rice in with the chicken stock. Let it come to a boil, place a lid on and turn the heat down to low for 10 mins.

Uncover, place the chicken thighs on top, seared side up, and drizzle over the marinade. Place the lid back on, and transfer into the oven for 10 mins. Then, remove the lid and leave it in the oven for another 7-10 minutes, until the chicken is fully cooked and starting to char in places.
Meanwhile, trim and finely slice the sugar snap peas and slice the carrots into thin matchsticks. Toss them all together with the sesame seeds. Right before serving, drizzle over some olive oil.
Once the chicken is cooked, remove the pan from the oven. Transfer the chicken to a board and let the rice rest for 5-10 mins before fluffing.

Once your chicken and rice are rested, slice the chicken. Divide the rice between Tupperware containers. Add the chicken on top, along with the slaw and nestle in a wedge of lime. Garnish with the remaining spring onions and box up. Stash in the fridge ready for later - these keep for up to 3 days.

name: Caramelised Aubergines & Coconut Cucumber Salad
steps: Slice the aubergines into 3cm chunks. Bash the ginger and garlic. Thinly slice the cucumber, add to a strainer and toss with a good pinch of salt. Thinly slice the chilli. Pick the coriander leaves and discard the stems.
Set a large frying pan over medium heat. Once hot, add the coconut and toast, stirring for 2-4 mins, until nicely golden. Transfer onto a plate and set aside.
Return the pan over high heat with a generous glug of olive oil. Once hot, chuck in the aubergines and cook for 5–7 mins, until golden.

Pour in the coconut water and soy sauce, then drop in the garlic and ginger. Bring to the boil, turn the heat down to medium and let it simmer for 10–15 mins until the aubergines are softened and jammy.

Mix the cornflour with the water until smooth, then pour into the aubergines. Stir together and let it come back to the boil. Cook for 2–4 mins until thickened. Season with salt and pepper. Add a splash more water if it’s too thick.

Taste the cucumber. If they’re too salty, rinse under cold water and drain well. Toss with the juice of the lime, most of the desiccated coconut (saving a sprinkle for the garnish) and a drizzle of olive oil. Season with again, if needed.

Reheat the rice according to pack instructions and divide between your lunch boxes. Remove the ginger from the aubergines, then spoon over the rice and add the cucumber salad. Finish with a sprinkle of toasted coconut, chilli and coriander. 
Once cooled, box up and pop in the fridge, ready for tomorrow’s lunch - they’ll keep for up to 3 days.

name: Marinated Tomato and Ricotta Pasta Salad
steps: Finely chop your tomatoes, then add them to a bowl. Grate in your garlic clove and lemon zest, then add the juice of ½ your lemon, 2 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt. Leave them to sit at room temperature.
Bring a large pan of water to a boil. Salt it well.
Pour your pasta into your water and cook it until al dente.
Meanwhile, finely chop your dill.
Add your ricotta to a bowl along with 2 tbsp olive oil and then grate in your parmesan. Give it a good whisk until it is totally smooth.
When your pasta is cooked, add a ladle of your pasta water to the ricotta mix, and whisk until it comes together.
Drain your pasta, then combine with your ricotta, tomatoes and herbs. Give it a good mix.

Divide between your Tupperware containers and top with a crack of black pepper in each. Once they've cooled a bit, box up and pop in the fridge.
These will keep for up to 3 days in the fridge.

name: Marry Me Halloumi Bowl
steps: Heat a large saucepan over medium heat. Add a splash of olive oil, then stir in the bulgur wheat. Fry for 2 mins until golden. Add the smoked paprika and cook for another 30 seconds. Cover with boiling water until 2cm above the bulgur, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cover and cook for 15 mins.
Make the tomato yoghurt dressing by blending the Greek yoghurt, sun-dried tomatoes, and lemon juice until smooth. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

Cut the halloumi into small 2cm-sized pieces. Heat a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the halloumi pieces and cook on all sides until golden and charred. Pour in the pomegranate molasses and let it bubble and thicken, coating the halloumi.
Assemble the bowl: toss the sliced cherry tomatoes and most of the torn basil through the cooked bulgur wheat. Season with salt and black pepper.
Divide the bulgur into serving boxes. Top with the glazed halloumi, tomato yoghurt dressing, and mixed seeds. Garnish with the remaining basil leaves.
Refrigerate until needed. No need to reheat before serving.

name: Tuna & Green Bean Chopped Salad
steps: Boil your green beans in water until soft, drain, and then allow to cool.
Chop and discard the heads off the pickled guindilla chillies. Add your beans to a chopping board along with your tuna and chillies and roughly chop them up.
Add in your capers and continue to chop.
Add all of your chopped ingredients to a bowl and squeeze in the juice from your lemons. Add in a good glug of olive oil and season generously with salt and pepper.
Divide the salad between Tupperware containers and box up. Pop in the fridge until needed - these will keep for up to 3 days.

name: Chicken, Pepper & Cucumber Chopped Salad
steps: Preheat your oven to 180°C. Season your chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper. Place your breasts onto a baking tray and get them in the oven for 25 mins. Allow them to cool once cooked – the salad doesn’t need to be warm.
Chop up the basil, the roasted red peppers, cucumbers, pistachios, and chicken into even-sized pieces. Toss together in a large bowl with kalamata olives.

Divide the salad between Tupperware containers with a dollop of cottage cheese in each box and pop them in the fridge. Keep the dressing separate – either pour a little over in the morning or stash it in a little pot inside your lunch box to add just before eating.

name: Honey Harissa Carrot Couscous with Feta Dressing
steps: Preheat the oven to 190°C fan. Halve the carrots lengthways and cut into 4cm pieces.
In a small bowl, mix the honey and harissa.
Toss the carrots with a splash of olive oil, cinnamon, salt, and black pepper. Spread onto a baking tray and roast for 20-25 mins.
Pat dry the chickpeas and add them to the baking tray. Roast for another 15 mins until crispy. Once cooked, toss with the harissa-honey mixture.
Meanwhile, place the couscous in a bowl, season with salt, and cover with boiling water. Place a plate on top to trap the steam and let sit for 5 mins. Fluff with a fork
Mix the couscous with chopped parsley and chopped olives Season to taste.
In a blender, blitz the feta, Greek yoghurt, and lemon juice until smooth. Season with salt and black pepper.
To serve, divide the couscous into serving boxes, top with the roasted carrots, roasted chickpeas, and drizzle with the feta dressing. Refrigerate until needed. No need to reheat before serving.

name: Pesto Salmon Orzo Salad
steps: Cut the courgette into irregular 2cm pieces. Add to a bowl, toss with olive oil, salt and black pepper, then tip into the air fryer basket. Cook at 200°C for 5 mins.

Pat the salmon dry then rub with olive oil, salt, black pepper and fennel seeds. Add the cherry tomatoes to the air fryer basket with the courgettes, then place the salmon on top, skin-side down. Reduce the heat to 180°C and cook for 8-10 mins, depending on the thickness of the salmon. If it’s not fully cooked, continue in one-minute bursts.
Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Drop in the orzo and cook following packet instructions.
In a large bowl (the same one from earlier to save on washing up), whisk together a glug of olive oil, the juice of the lemon, Dijon mustard and a pinch of salt and black pepper.
Roughly chop the parsley. Remove the salmon from the air fryer and set aside. Tip the roasted veg into the dressing along with the drained orzo and parsley. Mix well.
Spoon the orzo salad into your Tupperware containers, flake the salmon over the top and finish with a drizzle of pesto. Box up and pop in the fridge (these last for up to 3 days). Lunch is done.

name: Healthy Chicken & Broccoli Chopped Salad
steps: Boil the broccoli in a pot of salted boiling water for 3-4 mins until it’s just about cooked. Remove the broccoli and allow it to cool.

Preheat your oven to 180°C. Season your chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper. Place your chicken breasts onto a baking tray and get them in the oven for 25 mins. Allow them to cool once cooked – the salad doesn’t need to be warm.
Heat up your quinoa according to package instructions.
Squeeze the juice from your limes and combine with the rest of the dressing ingredients in a bowl.
Chop up the coriander, the cooked broccoli, and chicken into even-sized pieces. Toss with the quinoa in a large bowl.

Divide the salad between your Tupperware containers and stick them in the fridge.Keep the dressing separate – either pour it over in the morning or stash it in a little pot inside your box to add just before eating.These will keep for up to 3 days in the fridge.

name: Herby Halloumi with Dilly Rice & Tzatziki
steps: Rinse the long grain rice under cold water until it runs clear. Pick and roughly chop the fronds of dill, and finely slice the stems. In a saucepan over medium heat, melt salted butter. Add orzo and toast for 3–4 mins until golden. Stir in the rice, pour over water and season with salt. Bring to a boil, cover, and reduce to low. Cook undisturbed for 12 mins. Remove from the heat and leave covered for 10 mins. Just before serving, fluff with a fork and stir through the dill fronds and stems.

In a spice grinder or pestle and mortar, grind nigella seeds, coriander seeds, Urfa chilli flakes and a pinch of black pepper to a fine powder. Stir the spice blend into honey and set aside. Halve each block of halloumi, then cut each half into 2 triangles. Heat a little olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat and fry the halloumi for 3–5 mins per side until golden. Transfer to a plate and drizzle over the spiced honey. Finish with a grating of lemon zest if you like.

Slice the courgettes into thick 3–4cm coins. Season with salt. Heat a generous amount of olive oil in the frying pan. Once hot, lay the courgettes cut-side down. Cook for 4–5 mins until well charred, then flip and cook for 2–3 mins more. Remove from the heat and let them sit in the pan for 5 mins to finish cooking through.

Make the tzatziki. Halve the cucumber lengthways and scoop out the seeds. Finely dice the flesh. Add to a bowl with yoghurt, grate in garlic, and finely chop the mint. Zest and juice the lemon into the mix, season with salt and pepper, and stir well.
Divide the rice between containers. Top with charred courgettes and halloumi. Serve with a dollop of tzatziki on the side or in a separate pot for freshness.

name: Greens, Eggs and Rice
steps: Preheat your oven to 220°C. Tear or slice the mushrooms into roughly 1cm chunks. Spread them out on a large baking tray. Sprinkle over the cumin, coriander, and sesame seeds. Drizzle with olive oil, season generously with salt, and toss to coat. Roast for 25–30 mins, or until golden and crisp around the edges.

Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then drain well. Blitz the spinach, water, garlic and butter in a blender until smooth and vibrant green. Tip the rice into a medium saucepan, pour over the spinach mixture, and bring to a boil. Cover with a tight-fitting lid, reduce the heat to the lowest setting, and cook for 12 mins. Turn off the heat and leave to steam for 10 mins. Fluff with a fork, mix through any settled spinach, and cover again for 5 mins. Season to taste.

Bring a medium saucepan of water to the boil. Lower in the eggs and boil for 7 mins. Transfer immediately to a bowl of ice water for a couple of minutes, then peel. Roll the eggs gently in toasted sesame seeds until fully coated.
Mix the dressing. In a small bowl, whisk together the kimchi brine, honey, peanut butter and vinegar. Slowly whisk in olive oil to emulsify. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Divide the green rice between containers. Top with roasted mushrooms and a sesame egg. Serve with the kimchi peanut dressing on the side.

name: Marinated Za'atar Beetroot, Feta & Minty Grains
steps: Dice ¾ of the beetroot into small chunks and toss in a bowl with the za’atar, two thirds of the balsamic vinegar, a splash of olive oil and a good pinch of salt. Set aside to marinate.

Roughly chop the remaining beetroot and add to a blender with the crème fraîche, remaining balsamic, the garlic clove, cumin, and a squeeze of lemon juice. Blitz until completely smooth. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Finely slice the roasted red peppers and set aside. Chop the mint finely, reserving a little for garnish.
Warm the grain pouches in the microwave according to the pack instructions, then tip into a large bowl. Stir through the red peppers, most of the mint, and a little lemon zest. Taste and season.

Spread a spoonful of the beetroot sauce on each plate. Top with a handful of lamb’s lettuce, a pile of the minty grains, spoonfuls of marinated beetroot, and crumbled feta. Finish with extra mint and a final drizzle of olive oil, if you fancy.

name: Sticky Aubergine Rice Bowl
steps: Preheat the oven to 170°C.

Slice the aubergines into batons and whack them in a colander.
Salt and leave for 5 mins to extract the water. After 5 mins, pat
dry and get them onto a baking tray. Drizzle with oil and place in the oven for 30 mins.

While your aubergine is roasting, prep your veg. Thinly slice the
spring onions, red cabbage, garlic, ginger and red chillies.

Grab two bowls. Add the spring onions to one and the red
cabbage to the other. Cover the spring onions with the juice of
the lime, a third of the rice vinegar and a sprinkling of salt.
Over the red cabbage pour another third of the rice vinegar,
half the sesame oil and a sprinkle of salt and mix it
through. Cover and place both in the fridge.

Rinse the sushi rice, then add to a saucepan with just enough
water to cover. Leave for 30 mins to soak.

Heat a drizzle of oil in a wok or large frying
pan and add the garlic, ginger and red chillies and fry over a low
heat. Once softened, add the hoisin sauce, soy sauce, sesame seeds, agave, veggie stock cube, chilli oil and the remaining sesame oil and rice vinegar. Give
everything a good mix together, then add the aubergine straight
from the oven.

Add enough water to just cover the aubergine and leave to
simmer until it has reduced into a lovely thick sauce. Stir often.

Drain the rice and add it to a saucepan with 480ml water (if you're adjusting the servings, use a ratio of one part rice to one and a half parts water) and the shichimi. Bring to the boil, then turn to a simmer, cover
with the lid and simmer until cooked, about 15 mins.

Time to build your lunch boxes. Divide the sushi rice between your Tupperware containers. Add a
generous dollop of aubergine sauce, a helping of marinated red
cabbage and some sliced avocado. Garnish with the spring onions,
the crispy chilli bits from the chilli oil and some more sesame seeds. 
Leave to cool, then box up and pop in the fridge ready for lunchtime. These will keep for up to 3 days in the fridge.

name: Chicken & Rice with Peanut Curry Sauce
steps: In a bowl, mix the chicken thighs with half the garlic (peeled and bashed) and the kecap manis. Season with salt and black pepper, then set aside to marinate.

Heat a drizzle of oil in a frying pan with high sides over medium heat. Once hot, add the marinated chicken and fry for 10-12 mins, turning occasionally, until cooked through and slightly charred. If your sauce is reducing too much turn the heat down to low. Transfer to a plate to rest.
Strip the cavolo nero leaves from their stems.
In the same pan, add the cavolo nero leaves and cook until wilted. Transfer to the chicken plate.
Add the remaining bashed garlic, red Thai curry paste, tomato purée, and peanut butter to the empty pan. Cook, stirring, for 2-3 mins until the mixture darkens in colour.
Pour in the coconut milk and cook, stirring, until the sauce thickens. Remove from heat and season with salt, lime juice, and a touch of sugar if needed.
Reheat the rice and divide it into serving boxes. Slice the chicken thighs and place them on top with the cavolo nero. Pour over the peanut curry sauce.
Garnish with crispy onions and fresh coriander. Box up and refrigerate until needed. Reheat before serving.

name: Spicy Peanut Air Fryer Salmon & Greens
steps: Cook the rice following packet instructions.

For the spice mix, finely chop or crush the peanuts and add to a large mixing bowl. Add the garlic powder, chilli powder, white pepper, sugar and sesame seeds and mix to combine. Transfer ¾ of the spice mix to a large plate, setting aside the rest for garnish.

Take your salmon and pop it on top of the spice mix, flesh side down. Press gently to coat, pressing it up the sides too. Drizzle the salmon with a little olive oil then transfer to the air fryer basket. Cook in the air fryer at 180°C for 8-10 mins or until cooked through (this will depend on the thickness of the salmon).

While the salmon is cooking, make the sauce. Add the peanuts to a high speed blender and blitz until you have a nice smooth sauce, scraping down the sides a few times if necessary. Halve the cherry tomatoes and deseed the chilli (or leave the seeds in if you like it spicy) then throw both into the blender and blitz until smooth. Taste and season with salt and the juice of the limes. Set aside.
Bring a pot of salted water to the boil. Drop in the green beans for 2 mins until tender, then drain and set aside.
Finely chop most of the coriander, saving some for garnish, and stir it through the cooked rice. Add the green beans to the rice and give it a mix to roughly combine.

Divide the rice and beans between Tupperware containers. Flake the salmon on top with the remaining spice mix. Scatter over the fresh coriander and nestle in a wedge of lime. Keep the sauce separate - either pour over in the morning of stash a little pot in your Tupperware box to add just before eating.Box up and pop in the fridge ready for later. These will keep for up to 3 days.

name: Chicken Meatballs with Herby Freekeh & Greens
steps: Pour the water into a saucepan and bring to the boil. While it heats, finely chop the parsley and the lemon. Stir in freekeh, cover, reduce the heat to low-medium, and simmer for 10–15 mins until the water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork, then stir through the parsley and lemon zest. Set aside to cool slightly.

Make the meatballs: Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a frying pan and fry 3 tbsp red curry paste for 3 mins until fragrant. Meanwhile, finely chop the coriander stalks and zest a lime. In a large bowl, combine chicken mince, the coriander stalks, lime zest, fish sauce, eggs, breadcrumbs, the fried curry paste, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Mix until sticky. Wet your hands and form into 12 meatballs (about 60–70g each).
Cook the meatballs: Wipe out the frying pan, add more oil, and fry the meatballs over medium heat for 10–15 mins, turning to brown evenly, until golden and cooked through.

Trim green beans and chop broccoli into small florets. Bring a pan of salted water to a rolling boil and blanch the veg for 3–4 mins until just tender. Drain and shock in iced water to keep their colour and crunch, then dry thoroughly.

In a large bowl, add pesto, grate in Parmesan, zest and juice a lemon, and drizzle in a few glugs of olive oil. Season well with salt and pepper. Add the drained greens and toasted almonds. Toss to coat.

Make the Jalapeño Yoghurt Dressing: Deseed and roughly chop the jalapeños. Add to a blender with Greek yoghurt, avocado, roughly chop fresh coriander, and the juice of the limes. Blend until smooth, scraping down the sides. Season with salt to taste.
Divide the freekeh between your lunchboxes. Top with chicken meatballs and the dressed greens. Serve with a generous spoonful of the yoghurt dressing or pack it on the side for drizzling later.

name: Everything-Seasoned Salmon with Spiced Cauliflower & Bulgur
steps: Preheat the oven to 160°C fan.

Make the bulgur base: Pour water and olive oil into a saucepan. Stir in the tomato purée and pomegranate molasses. Season with salt and bring to the boil. Once boiling, stir in bulgur wheat. Return to the boil, cover, and turn the heat to low. Simmer for 10 mins until the water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork, then stir through the juice of the lemon. Taste and season again if needed.
In a bowl, mix the poppy seeds, white sesame seeds, black sesame seeds, garlic powder, onion powder, and a pinch of salt.
Pat the salmon fillets dry with kitchen paper. Press the flesh side only into the seasoning mix to coat evenly. Set aside.

Cut the cauliflower into rough florets. Peel the red onions and cut into chunky wedges. Tip the cauliflower and onion into a large roasting tray with unpeeled garlic cloves. Sprinkle over the turmeric, ground coriander, and season generously. Drizzle with olive oil and toss everything to coat. Roast for 20 mins.
Remove the tray from the oven. Nestle the salmon fillets in, skin-side down. Drizzle with a little olive oil and return to the oven for 10–15 mins, or until the salmon is cooked through and flaky.
Make the dressing. In a small bowl or jar, mix olive oil with balsamic vinegar to taste. Season with salt and pepper.

Divide the bulgur into containers. Top with the roasted cauliflower, onions, and garlic. Place a salmon fillet on top of each. Serve with the balsamic dressing drizzled over, or pack it separately if storing.

name: Crunchy Quinoa, Chicken & Bean Salad
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Put the chicken thighs into a bowl. Finely grate the garlic over the chicken and squeeze in the lemon juice. Add the oregano, drizzle with olive oil and generously season. Mix and set aside.
Tip the quinoa onto a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil and season. Toss together and bake for 15-20 mins. The quinoa will crisp-up as it cools.

Meanwhile, strip the stems off the cavolo nero, tear the leaves into bite-sized chunks and transfer to a bowl. Season with salt and scrunch together until the cavolo nero wilts. Thinly slice the spring onions, drain the cannellini beans and toss both through the cavolo nero.
Add all the dressing ingredients to a blender and blend until smooth. Taste and season.
Place a frying pan over a medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, fry the chicken on both sides (10-15 mins in total) until golden brown and cooked through.
Toss three-quarters of the crispy quinoa through the bean mixture with 2 tbsp of the dressing. Slice the chicken.

Share the salad between meal-prep containers, top with the chicken and drizzle over some more dressing. Sprinkle with the remaining crispy quinoa and parsley leaves. It will keep in the fridge for 3 days.

name: Spanakopita Halloumi Bowl
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C. Tip the pine nuts onto a baking tray and roast for 10-12 mins until golden.

Meanwhile, finely chop the red onion and garlic. Heat a splash of olive oil in the biggest pot you have set over a medium heat. Add the onion and fry for 5-7 mins then add the garlic and cook for another 2 mins.
Add the spinach a big handful at a time, stirring until wilted before adding another handful. Once all the leaves are wilted in the pan, remove the spinach mix to a plate and set aside to cool.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil then add the giant couscous. Reduce to a simmer and cook the couscous for 8 mins, then drain and transfer to a large salad bowl.
Meanwhile, break the halloumi down its natural split and dice into 2cm pieces. Heat a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the halloumi, cooking on all sides until golden.

Squeeze as much of the liquid out of the spinach mix as you can, then finely chop and add to the couscous. Finely chop the dill, parsley and mint, and set aside a small handful for garnish, then add the rest to the couscous and mix to combine. Grate in the zest of the lemon with a squeeze of the juice and the sumac, then season with salt and pepper.

Divide the couscous between Tupperware containers and top each with halloumi, a dollop of yoghurt, roasted pine nuts and remaining fresh herbs.Box up and pop in the fridge ready for lunch. These will keep for up to 3 days.

name: Spicy Salmon Bowl with Sesame Rice & Soy Butter Spinach
steps: Wash the sushi rice until the water runs clear. Add the rinsed rice to a saucepan along with the water. Set the pan over a high heat and let the water come to the boil then cover with a lid, turn the heat down to low and leave to cook for 12 mins. Then turn the heat off and leave it covered, undisturbed for another 10 mins.

For the sauce, grate the garlic into a large bowl then add the remaining sauce ingredients and whisk until incorporated. Dice the salmon fillets into large cubes (about 3 per fillet) and add them to the sauce. Toss well to cover then transfer to a container and leave to marinate in the fridge.

Now let’s make the rice seasoning. In a small bowl, whisk together the salt, sugar and vinegar and set aside. In a blender, blitz the nori into small pieces or cut into small pieces. Once the rice is cooked, stir through the seasoning liquid, nori and sesame seeds.

For the spinach, thinly slice the garlic. Melt the butter in a medium saucepan set over a medium heat then add the sliced garlic and cook for about 3 mins until softened and fragrant. Add the spinach and gently wilt before seasoning with the soy sauce and a squeeze of lemon.
When you want to eat, pop the salmon in the air fryer and pour over the sauce. Cook at 240°C for 3-4 mins. Heat the rice in the microwave until piping hot, if needed. Thinly slice the spring onions.

Divide the rice into your Tupperware containers, top with the salmon. Finish with the buttery spinach, spring onions and some extra nori, if you like. Box up and pop in the fridge until needed. These will keep for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Miso Butter Roast Chicken & Radishes
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C fan. Make sure your butter is at room temperature.

Generously season the chicken thighs with salt and black pepper. Place them skin-side down into an ovenproof frying pan over medium heat. Cook undisturbed for 8-10 minutes until the skin is golden brown. Transfer to a plate, skin-side up.
In the same pan, add the halved radishes and mushrooms sliced into 1cm-sized chunks. Stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until golden brown.
Pour in the chicken stock and rice vinegar, bring to a boil, then place the chicken skin-side up back on top.
Transfer the pan to the oven and roast for 25-30 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked.
Reheat the rice and divide it into serving boxes.
Once the chicken is cooked, place it on top of the rice with the roasted vegetables.
Whisk the miso, mirin, butter, and half the sesame seeds into the pan juices. Drizzle over the chicken and rice.
Finish with the remaining sesame seeds and serve.

name: Hot Smoked Salmon Bowl with Miso Lemon Vinaigrette
steps: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Meanwhile, halve any larger Jersey potatoes so they’re all roughly the same size. Once the water’s boiling, add the potatoes and cook for 10–15 mins until a knife slides in easily. Drain and set aside to cool slightly.

Peel and finely slice the red onion. Add to a small bowl, squeeze over the juice of ¼ of the lemon and add a pinch of sea salt. Massage with your hands for 30 seconds to soften and lightly pickle. Set aside.
Finely chop the chives. In a large mixing bowl, stir together the Greek yoghurt, chopped chives, half the wholegrain mustard, and a good pinch of salt and pepper.
Once the potatoes are cool enough to handle, toss them into the yoghurt mix and stir until well coated.
In a small bowl, whisk together the miso paste, remaining lemon juice, white wine vinegar, olive oil, remaining mustard, and honey. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Thinly slice the cucumber. Rinse and dry the spinach. Flake the hot smoked salmon into bite-sized chunks, removing any skin if needed.

Divide the spinach and cucumber between bowls or containers. Add a generous scoop of potato salad, then top with the flaked salmon and quick-pickled onions. Finish with a good drizzle of the miso vinaigrette.

name: Seedy Feta & Giant Couscous Salad
steps: Bring a saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the giant couscous and cook for 6 mins, or until tender. Drain and rinse under cold water. Finely slice the red onion and pick the parsley and dill. Toss the herbs and onion through the couscous with the spinach and a generous squeeze of lemon juice. Season well with salt and pepper.

Slice the courgettes into 3–4cm-thick coins. Heat a large frying pan over high heat and add enough olive oil to coat the base. Season the courgette coins with salt and place cut-side down into the pan. Fry for 4–5 mins until blistered and charred, then flip and cook the other side for 2–3 mins. Turn off the heat and leave them to sit in the pan for 5 mins.

Preheat the grill to high. Tip the seeds onto a plate and season with black pepper. Press each side of the feta into the seeds so they stick. Place the seeded feta on a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil, and grill for 3–4 mins until golden and lightly crisp.
Make the creamy green dressing. Add the avocado, anchovies, lime juice, chives, basil, kefir and olive oil to a blender. Blitz until smooth and creamy. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Spoon the couscous mixture into containers. Top with chunks of seedy feta and blistered courgette. Serve with the green dressing on the side.

name: Chicken & Cherry Tomato Barley Salad
steps: Rinse the pearl barley under cold water. Tip into a saucepan with water and a good pinch of salt. Bring to the boil, cover with a lid, reduce the heat to low, and cook for around 40 mins, or until tender. Add a splash more water if needed. Drain off any excess water and fluff with a fork.

Add the chicken to a bowl. Finely grate in the garlic, add the Dijon mustard and lemon juice. Season well with salt and plenty of black pepper. Mix to coat. Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the chicken for 10–15 mins, turning occasionally, until golden and cooked through. Set aside to rest, then slice.

Peel and finely slice the shallots into rings. Tip into a bowl with the vinegar and let sit for 5 mins to lightly pickle. Roughly chop the tomatoes and add them to the bowl. Thinly slice the courgette and pit the cherries, then add both to the salad. Season well with salt and pepper, tear in the dill, and drizzle with a little olive oil. Let the salad sit for at least 30 mins to develop flavour.

Make the green chilli dressing. Crack open the cardamom pods and remove the seeds. Toast the cardamom seeds, cumin seeds, and coriander seeds in a dry pan over medium heat for 2–3 mins, until fragrant. Transfer to a blender and pulse until roughly broken down. Add the trimmed chillies, garlic, and fresh coriander. Blend while gradually pouring in the olive oil to emulsify. Squeeze in the lemon juice, season with salt and pepper, and blend again until smooth.
Divide the barley between containers. Top with sliced chicken and a generous spoonful of the tomato and cherry salad. Drizzle with the green chilli dressing or serve it on the side.

name: Roast Sweet Potato Salad with Gochujang Tahini Sauce
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C fan. Cut the sweet potatoes into wedges.
In a bowl, toss the sweet potato wedges with a splash of olive oil, salt, black pepper, and cumin. Spread onto a baking tray.
In the same bowl, toss the chickpeas with the remaining oil and seasoning left in the bowl. Set aside.
Roast the sweet potatoes for 25 mins. Flip the potatoes, add the chickpeas to the tray, and roast for another 15 mins until golden and crisp.

Make the dressing: In a bowl, whisk together the gochujang, tahini, soy sauce, maple syrup, and lime juice. Loosen with a little water until it reaches a drizzleable consistency. Taste and season with salt, if needed.
Place the kale in a colander and pour over boiling water until wilted. Squeeze out excess liquid, roughly chop, and mix through the lentils.

To serve, divide the lentil mixture into serving boxes. Top with roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas. Drizzle with the gochujang tahini sauce and garnish with toasted sesame seeds and sliced spring onions.

name: Crispy Sesame Feta, Roast Figs & Lemon Quinoa
steps: Bring a saucepan of salted water to the boil. Cook the quinoa according to the pack instructions. Drain well and set aside.

Halve each block of feta lengthways to make thinner slabs, then cut each piece into quarters — you should have 8 even slices. Tip the sesame seeds onto a plate and press each piece of feta into the seeds to coat one side. Set aside.

Finely chop the mint. Zest and juice the lemon. Toss the drained quinoa with chickpeas, lemon zest, and chopped mint. In a small bowl, whisk the lemon juice with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Drizzle over the quinoa and mix well.

Halve the figs and drizzle with a little olive oil and a pinch of salt. Air-fry at 180°C for 3–5 mins until soft and juicy. Remove the figs and add the sesame-coated feta. Air-fry at 200°C for 5 mins until golden and crispy.
Mix the honey with the balsamic vinegar and chilli flakes. Drizzle generously over the warm figs.
Spoon the quinoa salad onto plates or into containers. Top with crispy sesame feta and honeyed figs. Serve warm, or enjoy cold as a lunchbox.

name: Herby Chicken, Pepper & Quinoa Salad
steps: Thinly slice the roasted peppers. Peel and finely slice the onion, then rinse it under cold water in a sieve until crisp. Pick the mint leaves. Toss the sliced onion, peppers, and mint together in a bowl with the balsamic vinegar and olive oil. Season well with salt and black pepper.

Rinse the quinoa under cold water until it runs clear. Tip into a saucepan with water and a good pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce the heat to low and cook for 15–20 mins, or until all the water is absorbed. Remove from the heat and let it steam with the lid on for 5 mins. Fluff with a fork.

Make the Zhoug dressing. Lightly crack the cardamom pods open using the back of your knife. Add the coriander seeds, cumin seeds and crushed cardamom pods into a small frying pan. Place on medium heat and toast until fragrant, 2-3 mins.
Remove the cardamom seeds and discard the pod.

Add the spices into a food processor or blender and blitz until they have broken down slightly (don’t let them become a fine powder). Trim the chillies and add them to the spices with the garlic clove, herbs (stems and all). Blend until broken down, then gradually add the olive oil, until emulsified. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

Place the chicken thighs in a bowl. Finely grate over the garlic, add the Dijon mustard and lemon juice, and season with salt and loads of black pepper. Mix well to coat. Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the chicken for 10–15 mins, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through. Rest for 5 mins, then slice.
Divide the quinoa between your containers. Top with sliced chicken and spoon over the pepper and mint salad. Serve with a pot of Zhoug dressing on the side.

name: Spiced Chicken With Chilli Tomato Salad & Zingy Tahini Dressing
steps: Heat a splash of olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the cashews and fry until golden. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on kitchen paper. Lower the heat, then add the mustard seeds and fry until they begin to pop. Add the urid dal, asafoetida, ginger, curry leaves, turmeric, and dried chillies. Fry for 3–4 mins until the lentils are golden. Remove from the heat and squeeze in the juice of the lemons. Stir through the cooked rice and cashews season well and set aside.

In a bowl, combine the grated garlic, sumac, Lebanese 7-spice, and a drizzle of olive oil. Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper, then add to the bowl and mix until coated. Heat a large frying pan with oil over medium-high heat. Cook the thighs for 8–10 mins, turning until deeply golden and cooked through. Rest briefly, then slice.
In a bowl, combine the chopped tomatoes with the finely sliced spring onions. Stir through the crispy chilli oil and rice vinegar. Season with salt and toss to coat. Set aside.

Add the unpeeled garlic cloves to a blender with lemon juice and cumin. Blend until smooth. Pour the purée into a fine mesh sieve set over a bowl and press to extract the liquid. Discard solids. Whisk in the tahini — it will seize and thicken. Add a splash of cold water at a time, whisking, until you reach a smooth, yoghurt-like consistency. Season with salt.
Divide the lemon rice between lunchboxes. Top with sliced chicken and spoonfuls of tomato salad. Pack the tahini dressing separately and drizzle on when serving.

name: Slow Roast Tomato & Egg Curry Rice
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C fan.
Toss the halved tomatoes with salt, garam masala, black pepper, and two-fifths of melted ghee or oil. Mix well and spread onto a baking tray.
Roast for 30-40 mins until soft and slightly caramelised.
Cook the rice according to package instructions.

Meanwhile, heat the remaining ghee in a pan over medium heat. Add the curry leaves, finely sliced garlic, nigella seeds, mustard seeds, and chopped chilli. Cook for 1-2 mins until fragrant, then remove from heat.
Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add the eggs and cook for 7 mins for soft yolks. Drain and cool under cold water before peeling.
In a bowl, mix the finely sliced red onions with lime juice and a pinch of salt. Massage gently with your hands and set aside to pickle.
To serve, divide the rice into bowls. Top with roasted tomatoes, eggs, coriander, and pickled onions. Drizzle the spiced ghee and roasting juices over the dish.

name: Roasted Halloumi and Pickled Citrus Grain Salad
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C fan.

Time to get prepared. Tear the halloumi into bite-sized shards. Dice the cucumber into 2cm-sized pieces. Thinly slice the shallots, segment your oranges and squeeze the juices remaining from the orange remnants into a bowl. Pick the leaves from the parsley and mint.
Line a baking tray with parchment paper. Place the cherry tomatoes on the tray and top with the torn halloumi. Roast for 10-15 minutes until the halloumi is golden and the tomatoes are tender.
Meanwhile, in a bowl, toss the shallots and orange segments with the reserved orange juice and lime juice. Let sit to pickle.
Add the parsley stems to a blender. Set the parsley and mint leaves aside.
For the dressing, add the mint, coriander, lime zest, lime juice, kefir, olive oil, and honey to the blender. Blend until smooth. Season to taste with salt and black pepper.
Reheat the grains and divide them into serving boxes.
Toss the pickled orange and shallots with the cucumber, roasted halloumi and tomatoes, then spoon over the grains.
Once cooled, scatter over the parsley and mint leaves. Drizzle with the kefir dressing and refrigerate until needed. No need to reheat before serving.

name: Poached Chicken, Garlic Rice & Spring Onion Sauce
steps: Make the rice. Wash the rice two or three times until the water runs clear. Roughly chop the shallots into chunks and peel the garlic cloves. Throw both into a food processor and pulse until finely chopped (or finely chop by hand).

Pop a medium sized saucepan over a medium heat and add the butter. Once melted, throw in the shallot and garlic mix and cook for 10-12 mins until caramelised. Add the salt and sugar and cook for a further minute. Deglaze the pan with the dark soy sauce, scraping up any browned bits on the bottom.
