Tip in the washed rice followed by the chicken stock. Bring to the boil then pop the lid on and reduce the heat to as low as possible. Cook for 12 mins, then turn the heat off and let sit for 15 mins.

For the chicken, pop the water, spring onions, garlic cloves and salt in a large saucepan, set over a high heat and bring to the boil. Once boiling, throw in the chicken breasts, bring back to a simmer, pop the lid on and turn off the heat. Leave untouched for 25 mins. The residual heat will cook the chicken. Then, using tongs, remove the chicken from the liquid and set aside to cool. Once cool enough to handle, slice the chicken.

For the sauce, finely slice the spring onions and mince the ginger. Add both to a heatproof bowl along with the salt, MSG and sugar. Heat the vegetable oil over a high heat in a small pan until smoking then carefully pour the hot oil over the spring onion mixture. Mix and set aside to marinate for at least 5 mins.
For the garnish, slice up the cucumber and set aside.

To store, divide the rice between Tupperware containers and top with the sliced chicken. Pop the cucumber in its own separate container and the spring onion sauce in another. Get everything in the fridge.

When ready to eat, pop the chicken and rice container, with the lid loosely on but not sealed, in the microwave for 60 seconds or until piping hot. Let it sit for another 60 seconds before removing the lid. Top with the spring onion sauce and some cucumber slices, and a drizzle of your favourite chilli oil.

name: Chilli Orange Roasted Feta & Fennel Grain Bowl
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C fan.
Tear your feta into 2cm-sized chunks. Thinly slice the red chilli, zest half the orange and segment the whole. Thinly slice the fennel and pick the leaves from the mint.
Place the feta on an oiled baking tray, drizzle with olive oil, and roast for 10-15 minutes until golden.
Now for the dressing. In a bowl, combine the shallots, orange segments, chilli, and sherry vinegar. Season with salt and let sit to pickle.
In another bowl, toss the pecans, mint leaves, cooked grains, lentils, and fennel with half the orange dressing.
In a small bowl, mix the yoghurt with the orange zest, a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and black pepper. Stir and set aside.
Stir the cumin seeds and honey into the remaining orange dressing. Once the feta is golden, pour this dressing over the feta and return to the oven for another 10-15 minutes until caramelised.
Divide the grain mixture into serving boxes and top with the chilli orange roasted feta. Finish with a dollop of orange yoghurt. Refrigerate until needed—no need to reheat before serving.

name: Romesco Chickpeas
steps: Peel and finely slice the garlic. Halve all the cherry tomatoes. Heat 1/4 of the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat, add the garlic and smoked paprika and cook for 2 mins, stirring regularly. Add the chickpeas, along with the water from the jar, and stir to combine.
Add the cherry tomatoes, then cover with a lid and cook for 10 mins.
Meanwhile, add most of the roasted almonds, the rest of the olive oil, and the other ingredients for the sauce into a blender. Season with plenty of salt and pepper and blitz into a smooth sauce.

Stir the sauce into the chickpeas, taste and season. Spoon into bowls or meal-prep boxes, top with feta, the rest of the roasted almonds, parsley and chilli flakes. It will keep in the fridge for 3 days.

name: Honey Garlic Chicken with Broccoli Rice
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Dice the broccoli into small pieces. Cook the rice following pack instructions, adding the broccoli 3 mins before the end of the cooking time.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the spring onions. Dice the chicken into 3cm pieces. In a bowl or flat tray, mix the garlic powder, chilli powder, flour and a pinch of salt.
Toss the chicken in the mix to coat evenly, then transfer to a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil. Slide into the hot oven to roast for 15-20 mins, until cooked through.

Mince the garlic then add to a bowl along with the gochujang, soy sauce, honey and the juice of the limes. Mix to combine then pour over the chicken and pop it back in the oven for another 5 mins until sticky.
Box or plate up the broccoli rice, top with the sticky chicken, and drizzle over any remaining sauce. Scatter over the spring onions and sesame seeds. It will keep well in the fridge for 3 days.

name: Halloumi Grains with Green Tahini
steps: Cut the courgettes into irregular 4cm pieces. Break the halloumi down its natural split, then cut into chunky pieces about the same size as the courgettes.
Heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the halloumi and cook on all sides until golden – no need for oil. Remove from the pan.
Add the olive oil to the pan, then fry the courgettes on both sides until charred. Remove and season with salt and black pepper.

For the dressing, add the basil, tahini, juice of the lemons, ½ the jalapeños and all the water to a blender and blitz until smooth. Season with salt and black pepper, then taste and adjust if needed.
Mix the quinoa with the courgettes and season with salt and black pepper. Thinly slice the remaining jalapeño.

Box or plate up the courgette quinoa and top with the halloumi and sliced jalapeño. If eating later, store the dressing separately in an airtight container. If eating now, drizzle the dressing over the top. Everything will keep well in the fridge for 3 days.

name: Spicy Tuna Rice Bowl
steps: Cook the rice following packet instructions.

Finely slice the spring onions and set aside. Peel and slice the avocado and set aside. Cut the nori into strips, if using and set aside. Finely slice the cucumber and add it to a bowl with the rice vinegar and a pinch of salt. Scrunch with your hands until slightly softened.
In a bowl, mix the drained tuna with the mayonnaise, sriracha, soy sauce, sesame oil and spring onions. Taste and adjust seasoning with more soy sauce or sriracha if needed.
Divide the rice between containers. Top with a big scoop of spicy tuna, pickled cucumber, avocado and nori, if using. Sprinkle with togarashi and drizzle with more sriracha, if you like.
Pop in the fridge for an easy, flavour-packed meal later. It will keep well in the fridge for 3 days.

name: Leek, Tenderstem & Feta Frittata
steps: Heat the oven to 180C. Tear the leftover flatbreads into large chunks and add them into a tray with 1 tbsp olive oil. Season with salt and bake for 10-15 mins until crispy. If you didn't save any flatbread, use any bread you have! If you're short on time you can skip this step.
Finely slice the broccoli stalks, then roughly chop the florets. Trim and thinly slice the leeks.

Add 3 tbsp of olive oil into a medium sized oven-safe frying pan on a medium-high heat. Add the leeks and broccoli to the pan, season with salt and fry until softened, 4-5 mins, then add the garlic and cook for a further 1 min.

Meanwhile, crack the eggs into a bowl, and season generously with salt and pepper. Finely chop most of the parsley(stalks and all), saving a few leaves for the salad, then add the chopped herbs to the eggs and whisk until incorporated.

Remove from the pan from the heat, space the veggies out into one layer and pour the eggs over, making sure to get into every nook. Crumble the feta over and bake for 20 mins, or until a knife comes out clean.

While the frittata cooks, zest the lemon and squeeze the juice of the zested lemon into a bowl add the kale, then drizzle 3 tbsp of olive oil, season with salt, pepper. Using your hands massage/squeeze for 3-4 mins, until the kale leaves wilt and are not as tough. Set aside.

Toss your croutons into the salad and drizzle with yoghurt. Top with the reserved parsley leaves and some extra feta, if you like. Slice up the frittata and serve on plates or in meal-prep boxes with a side of salad.

name: Speedy Smoky Harissa Butter Beans
steps: Add the cherry tomatoes to a pan with a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Set it over a medium-high heat and cook for about 5 mins until starting to soften and burst open. Add a splash of water if they’re catching on the bottom of the pan.
Mince the garlic and add it to the tomatoes in the pan along with the tomato paste, ¾ of the harissa and the smoked paprika.

Add the tinned butterbeans and ½ their liquid to the pan then stir in the vegan cream cheese. Bring the mixture to a boil then turn down the heat and simmer for 5-10 mins until the beans have softened and the broth has thickened (it should be creamy).
Meanwhile, toast the bread and finely chop the herbs.
Ladle the beans into bowls or meal-prep boxes. Drizzle over the tahini and some remaining harissa. Finish with the chopped herbs and flaked almonds. It will keep in the fridge for 3 days.

name: Chicken, Spinach & Cheddar Soup
steps: Finely slice the red onion and add to a bowl with the juice of ¼ the lemon and a pinch of salt. Mix and set aside.

Finely dice the white onion and celery, and mince the garlic. Melt the butter in a large saucepan set over a medium heat. Add the onion and celery and cook for 6-7 mins until soft and jammy. Add the garlic, coriander and chilli flakes and cook for another 3-4 mins, until the garlic is soft.

Add the frozen spinach and chicken stock and bring to a gentle simmer. Once the spinach has defrosted and the broth is simmering, add the chicken thighs and gently simmer for 20 mins until cooked through. Then, remove the chicken and use two forks to shred.
Pour the broth mixture into a blender then add the fresh spinach and grate in the Cheddar. Blend on high until vivid green and smooth. Season to taste with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
To serve, add the shredded chicken to a bowl and pour over the broth. Top with the pickled onions, a crack of black pepper and some extra grated Cheddar, if you like. Serve with toasted sourdough.

If batch cooking for the week, transfer the leftover chicken and broth to a container and the pickled onions to another. It will keep in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat the chicken and broth together until piping hot before serving.

name: Proper Tomato Soup
steps: Peel the onion and carrot and dice into 1cm cubes. Add the butter to a large saucepan over a medium heat, then add the onion and carrots along with a big pinch of salt. Fry gently for 10 mins until softened.

Finely chop the garlic and add it to the pan along with the tomato paste and fry for 2 more min. Add the tomatoes and use your spoon to break them up in the pan, refill one of the cans of tomatoes with water and add to the pan along with the stock cube and the sugar. Bring to the boil, then turn to a simmer and cook for 40 mins.
Use a stick blender to blitz into a smooth purée, taste, and season with the vinegar. Add the cream and gently reheat.
Tip into meal-prep containers. Store in the fridge for up to 3 days until ready to reheat and eat. Top with some extra grated Cheddar cheese and a crack of black pepper if you like.

name: Immunity Ginger, Turmeric & Coconut Lentils
steps: Peel the butternut squash. Chop butternut squash and carrot into bite-size 2cm pieces. Dice onion and garlic cloves, grate the ginger, and shred the kale.

Heat a good glug of olive oil on a non-stick saucepan over a medium heat. Once hot, add the onion and fry until it begins to develop some colour. Add the garlic and ginger with a pinch of salt and let cook for another 2 mins until fragrant.
Add the turmeric and cumin and let the spices toast for a minute but don’t let them burn. If the pan is too dry, add a ladleful of vegetable stock.
Stir through the carrots, butternut squash, the remaining vegetable stock and coconut milk and leave to simmer for 25 mins until the carrots and the squash are tender.

Add the split lentils and leave to simmer, stirring regularly, for another 10 mins or until the lentils are fully cooked. The lentils will absorb a lot of the liquid so if it gets too dry, add a couple more ladles of water or vegetable stock.
Turn off the heat and mash about ⅓ of the carrot and squash chunks with a fork.
Stir through the nutritional yeast, the juice of the lemon and the shredded kale. Continue stirring until the kale just starts to wilt. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Divide between meal-prep containers. Store in the fridge for up to 3 days until ready to reheat and eat. Serve with 2 slices of toasted sourdough each.

name: Brothy Chickpeas with Chorizo & Cavolo Nero
steps: Grab a large saucepan and set it over a medium heat to preheat.

Dice the onions and finely slice the garlic and chilli. Add the onion to the pan with a shot of olive oil and a good pinch of salt. Cook for 3-4 mins then add the garlic, chilli and bay leaves. Cook for another min or two.

Halve the potatoes and strip the leaves from the cavolo nero stalks. Add them to the pan and cover with chicken stock. Add the chickpeas and bring the whole lot to the boil. Add a lid and let it bubble away for 20 mins.
Meanwhile, cut the chorizo into 1cm-thick coins and add to a small pan with a shot of olive oil. Set over a medium-low heat and let crisp up, drawing out all the bright red fat.
Remove the lid from the stew, season with salt and lemon jucie and finish with chopped dill.
Spoon into meal-prep containers and top with the chorizo. Keep in the fridge for 3 days until ready to eat and reheat.

name: Aubergine & Curried Sesame Noodle Salad
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan.
Trim and dice the aubergines into 2cm chunks. Spread out on a baking tray, drizzle with olive oil and season well. Roast for 20–25 mins until golden and creamy inside.
Meanwhile, cook the rice noodles following pack instructions. Once soft, run them under cold water in a sieve to chill them down, then toss with the chilli oil until coated.
Pick the coriander leaves and set aside. Save the stems for the dressing.

Chuck the tahini, coriander stems, ice cubes, curry powder, maple syrup and juice of the limes into a blender. Blitz until smooth. Taste, season with salt, and add more maple if you want it sweeter. The dressing should be runny, it’ll thicken slightly as it rests.
To box up, pour the dressing into the base of your containers. Pile the chilli noodles on top, followed by the roasted aubergine, and finish with the coriander leaves.
Chill until needed. Shake well before serving.

name: Instant Mushroom Miso Ramen
steps: Use a speed peeler to peel the carrot into thin ribbons. Finely slice the shiitake mushrooms and the spring onions. Chop up your tofu into even-sized cubes.
Add ¼ of the miso, soy sauce, sesame oil and chilli flakes into each pot and stir to combine. Layer the rest of the ingredients into the pots. You can break up the noodles if needed.
When ready to eat, add 470ml of boiling water to each pot and set aside for 5 mins to cook the noodles and soften the veg.

name: Pesto Minestrone Soup
steps: This recipe was written to make 4 servings.
Chop the Tenderstem broccoli into small pieces. Finely chop all of the herbs. Drain the beans.
Add a ¼ of the pesto, nutritional yeast, chili flakes and miso with a little salt and pepper into each pot and stir well to combine.
Layer up the veggies and beans and top with the almonds.
When ready to serve, pour over about 300ml of boiling water and set aside for 5-8 mins to soften.

name: Tomatoey Harissa Couscous Pots
steps: Finely chop the onion and the sun-dried tomatoes. Drain the chickpeas.
Add a quarter of the harissa and tomato purée along with a drizzle of the sun-dried tomato oil into the bottom of each container with some salt and pepper. Stir to combine.
Layer a quarter of the couscous over the harissa sauce and then a quarter of the rest of the ingredients.
When you are ready to eat, add 240ml of boiling water per pot. Stir and tip out onto a plate, give it a stir and enjoy.
